meta.title: Programa de Inglês Executivo
meta.subtitle: Desenho Curricular · 108 aulas · 7 módulos
meta.tagline: Inglês executivo para a Diretoria — visão, governança e negociação.
meta.particularity: Programa de Diretoria: do posicionamento estratégico à condução comercial de ponta a ponta. O encerramento integra tudo na jornada de um empreendimento — proposta, execução técnica e avaliação de retorno — conduzida por você em inglês.

overview: Um programa de inglês executivo desenhado para a sua atuação na Diretoria — conversas estratégicas, frentes comerciais e a condução de reuniões de alto nível com clientes internacionais. Ao longo do curso você constrói desde a base da identidade executiva em inglês (visão, governança e gestão de risco) até a aplicação prática em negociações, propostas e relacionamento de longo prazo. Todo o conteúdo vive no universo real da Racional, e o programa se encerra com você conduzindo, em inglês, a jornada completa de um grande empreendimento.
logic: A cada quatro aulas de conteúdo aprofundado (CORE), a quinta aula é uma aula de tom mais leve (BRIDGE) — extraída dos módulos de Relacionamento (M5) ou de Cultura Americana (M6) — preservando o engajamento ao longo das 108 aulas. As três aulas finais (CAPSTONE) consolidam o aprendizado em apresentações conduzidas pelo executivo, em cenário integrado de construção de um shopping center para cliente norte-americano.

legend.desc: Aula de conteúdo principal — desenvolvimento técnico, comercial ou executivo.
Aula intercalada — relacionamento e cultura, intercaladas para preservar o engajamento.
Apresentação final do executivo — aplicação integrada de tudo que foi aprendido.

modules.name: DIRETORIA EXECUTIVA
modules.objective: Desenvolver vocabulário e fluência em inglês para que o executivo se posicione com naturalidade em conversações estratégicas — visão corporativa, governança, gestão de risco, condução de mudanças e influência sobre stakeholders. Estabelece a base linguística da identidade executiva, antes da aplicação prática nos módulos seguintes.

modules.name: FRENTES COMERCIAIS
modules.objective: Cobrir o ciclo comercial em inglês de ponta a ponta — do funil de vendas ao fechamento do contrato e à gestão pós-venda. Capacita o executivo a atuar nas pré-vendas em parceria com a área comercial, defender margem em discussões com clientes, analisar e debater propostas, e conduzir o relacionamento com key accounts internacionais ao longo dos 18 a 24 meses típicos de cada projeto.

modules.name: ENGENHARIA CIVIL & CONSTRUÇÃO
modules.objective: Construir o vocabulário técnico aplicado ao setor — abrangendo os segmentos de atuação da Racional (escritórios, hospitais, shopping centers, data centers e indústria), os estágios da obra, procurement, controle de qualidade e gestão de prazo. Permite ao executivo integrar a terminologia técnica em conversações comerciais abrangentes e conduzir site visits com clientes internacionais sem perda de fluência.

modules.name: REUNIÕES & BUSINESS ENGLISH
modules.objective: Aplicar o inglês nas situações reais de interação executiva — reuniões mensais e quinzenais com clientes, war rooms, negociações de escopo, preço e prazo, conversas difíceis e comunicação por escrito e telefone. É o módulo em que o conteúdo absorvido nos módulos 1 a 3 se converte em ação verbal em tempo real. Apresenta-se pontualmente já na Aula 21 (Chairing meetings) e passa a dominar a sequência a partir da Aula 74.

modules.name: RELACIONAMENTO EM ENCONTROS DE NEGÓCIOS
modules.objective: Desenvolver a fluência conversacional para os momentos de relacionamento que cercam as reuniões formais — small talk, jantares de negócios, esportes, família e viagens. Habilita o executivo a construir vínculos de longo prazo com clientes internacionais ao longo do ciclo de 18 a 24 meses de cada projeto, transitando com naturalidade entre o registro profissional e o pessoal. Distribuído nas aulas 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 e 100.

modules.name: EUA & CULTURA AMERICANA
modules.objective: Oferecer o repertório cultural necessário para conversações com o cliente predominante da Racional (norte-americano) — incluindo cultura corporativa, política, economia, esportes, mídia e humor. Diferencia uma comunicação meramente funcional de uma interação que gera conexão genuína. Distribuído nas aulas 5, 15, 25, 35, 45, 55, 65, 75, 85, 95 e 105.

modules.name: ENCERRAMENTO — JORNADA DO SHOPPING CENTER
modules.objective: Encerrar o curso com três apresentações conduzidas pelo executivo dentro de um cenário integrado — um cliente norte- americano que contrata a Racional para a construção de um shopping center. As três aulas acompanham a jornada completa do projeto: pitch comercial, execução técnica e entrega final com avaliação de ROI. Funcionam simultaneamente como avaliação aplicada e como demonstração concreta de domínio do conteúdo.

capstoneDetail.title: Pitch comercial do shopping center
capstoneDetail.scenario: Cenário: cliente norte-americano busca a Racional para construir um shopping center. O executivo apresenta a empresa, cases comparáveis de empreendimentos já entregues, capacidade técnica, condições comerciais e estrutura da proposta, com o objetivo de fechamento do contrato.

capstoneDetail.title: Desenho técnico e execução do projeto
capstoneDetail.scenario: Cenário: contrato fechado. O executivo detalha o desenho do shopping center (layout, sistemas estruturais, MEP, vertical transportation), o cronograma com critical path, marcos de obra, gestão de fornecedores e o plano de execução até o handover.

capstoneDetail.title: Entrega, avaliação de custos e ROI
capstoneDetail.scenario: Cenário: obra concluída. O executivo apresenta o relatório final ao cliente: cost vs. budget, indicadores de qualidade e prazo, ROI projetado do empreendimento (foot traffic, lojas-âncora, revenue projections) e oportunidades de expansão futura.

lessons.title: Strategic vision & long-term planning
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue falar, em inglês simples, sobre a visão e o planejamento de longo prazo da Racional diante de um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
Strategic vision is the clear answer to a question that every North American client asks sooner or later: "Where does your company want to be five years from now?". As a member of Racional's Executive Board, you are not talking about a single project; you are talking about the direction of the company. The key terms here are vision, strategy and long-term. Mastering these words in English allows you to position yourself as a leader, and not only as a supplier.

In Racional's day-to-day, this comes up all the time. Project cycles last 18 to 24 months, and relationships with key accounts such as Microsoft, Amazon and Google span many years. When you say, in English, what the company's goal is and in which segments it will grow — offices, hospitals, shopping centers, hyperscale data centers and industry —, the client understands that they are dealing with a stable partner, with more than 50 years of history, 620+ projects and 10 million m² built.

That is why this first lesson builds the foundation of your executive identity in English. You will learn how to state the vision, how to talk about the plan for the coming years, and how to connect today's decisions to a larger goal. You don't need long sentences or jargon: you need the right words, said with confidence and simplicity.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar três frases-âncora simples: "Our vision is to be the best partner.", "This is a long-term plan." e "We want to grow in data centers."

Repare que tudo está no presente simples e com palavras curtas. É assim que você soa claro e seguro em inglês, sem complicar.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião de estratégia, um cliente norte-americano pergunta onde a Racional quer estar em cinco anos. Você responde com uma visão simples e confiante.
lessons.context: Our vision is to be the best partner in Brazil. We think long-term. We have a clear plan for the next five years. We want to grow in data centers and hospitals. The demand is strong there. Every decision today follows this goal.

vocab.example: Our vision is clear.
This is a long-term plan.
Our strategy is simple.
Our goal is to be the best.
We have a five-year plan.
We want to grow in data centers.
We want to lead the market.
We are a strong partner.
We plan for the next five years.
The demand for data centers is strong.
Hospitals are a key segment.
We give real value to clients.
Year three is a big milestone.
We focus on big projects.

exercises.title: 1. Termos da visão estratégica
exercises.explanation: São as quatro palavras centrais para falar de estratégia em inglês simples.

exercises.title: 2. Falando do prazo
exercises.prompt: Um executivo que fala dos "próximos cinco anos" está mostrando um pensamento:

options.text: long-term
invoice
options.whyWrong: 'Invoice' é fatura, não tem relação com prazo.

options.text: coffee break
options.whyWrong: 'Coffee break' é uma pausa, não um horizonte de planejamento.

exercises.explanation: 'Long-term' significa de longo prazo — perfeito para falar de estratégia.

exercises.title: 3. Complete a visão
exercises.prompt: Our ___ is to be the best partner in Brazil.
exercises.explanation: 'Our vision is to...' é a forma clássica de declarar para onde a empresa vai.

exercises.title: 4. Sua visão para a Racional
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 a 3 frases simples sobre a visão da Racional. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês da aula (por exemplo vision, plan, to grow, long-term).
exercises.modelAnswer: Our vision is to be the best partner in Brazil. This is a long-term plan. We want to grow in data centers.
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos da aula, não a perfeição da frase.

exercises.title: 5. Diga a sua visão em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Our vision is to be the best partner. We think long-term.
exercises.translation: Nossa visão é ser o melhor parceiro. Pensamos no longo prazo.
exercises.prompt: Imagine que o cliente acabou de perguntar sobre o futuro da empresa. Responda com firmeza e calma.
exercises.explanation: Frases curtas e claras passam mais segurança do que frases longas e complicadas.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por uns 15 a 20 segundos, diga ao cliente qual é a visão da Racional e em quais segmentos a empresa quer crescer nos próximos cinco anos.
takeaways: I can say our vision in simple English.
I can talk about a long-term plan.
I can say where we want to grow.
I can sound clear and confident with short sentences.

pill.sample: I'll park the car near the office before the meeting.

lessons.title: Leadership styles & corporate culture
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue descrever, em inglês simples, o seu estilo de liderança e a cultura da Racional para um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
Leadership style and company culture say a lot about what it will be like to work with Racional. North American clients value clear leaders, who take responsibility and give their team autonomy. The key terms here are leadership, culture and to lead by example. Knowing how to talk about this in English shows the client the kind of company they are hiring.

At Racional, with more than 50 years and hundreds of projects delivered, culture is a real differentiator. In long projects, lasting 18 to 24 months, the client wants to know whether people take ownership and whether there is accountability at every stage, from feasibility to delivery. As a member of the Board, you represent this culture when you talk with Microsoft, Amazon or Google.

This lesson gives you simple words to describe how you lead and how the team works. You will learn how to say that you trust the team, that you set the example, and that you hold people to results in a fair way. No difficult terms: just short sentences that convey confidence and clarity to the client.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar frases simples como "I lead by example.", "I trust my team." e "Our culture is strong."

São frases curtas, no presente simples, que mostram o seu estilo sem complicar.
lessons.situation: Num jantar de negócios, um cliente norte-americano pergunta como você lidera o seu time. Você responde de forma simples e direta.
lessons.context: I lead by example. I trust my team. I give them ownership of the project. Our culture is strong and clear. People take responsibility here. I am direct, but I am also easy to talk to.

vocab.example: Good leadership builds trust.
My leadership style is simple.
I lead a big team.
I always lead by example.
I trust my team.
I trust my people.
I give my team ownership.
We have clear accountability.
People take responsibility here.
Our culture is strong.
I delegate small tasks.
I am direct with my team.
I try to be approachable.
Our values are clear.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva
exercises.correctText: I lead by example and I trust my team.
exercises.explanation: Frase simples no presente que descreve um estilo de liderança claro.

exercises.title: 2. Monte a frase
exercises.explanation: Ordem básica em inglês: sujeito + verbo + objeto (I trust my team).

exercises.title: 3. Complete sobre liderança
exercises.prompt: I always lead by ___.
exercises.explanation: 'To lead by example' = liderar pelo exemplo, fazendo aquilo que se pede ao time.

exercises.title: 4. Senso de dono
exercises.prompt: Quando você dá ao time o sentimento de dono do projeto, você dá:

options.text: ownership
a coffee
options.whyWrong: 'A coffee' é um café, não tem a ver com responsabilidade.

options.text: a problem
options.whyWrong: 'A problem' é um problema; o sentido aqui é positivo.

exercises.explanation: 'Ownership' é o senso de dono — quando a pessoa cuida do resultado como se fosse seu.

exercises.title: 5. Descreva seu estilo em voz alta
exercises.targetText: I lead by example. I trust my team and I am direct.
exercises.translation: Eu lidero pelo exemplo. Confio no meu time e sou direto.
exercises.prompt: Responda como se o cliente tivesse perguntado: "How do you lead your team?"
exercises.explanation: Diga com calma; o tom direto agrada o cliente norte-americano.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por uns 15 a 20 segundos, descreva o seu estilo de liderança e a cultura da Racional usando palavras simples como lead, trust, ownership e culture.
takeaways: I can describe my leadership style in simple English.
I can say that I trust my team.
I can talk about ownership and accountability.
I can describe our company culture.

watch: Priorize a FALA: o aluno deve falar na maior parte da aula.

pill.tip: Curiosamente, em Boston às vezes aparece um 'r' onde não havia escrito, ligando duas vogais. "Idea is" sai como "idear is", inserindo um 'r' entre "idea" e "is".
pill.sample: The idea is great, but the data is still missing.

lessons.title: Decision-making under uncertainty
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue falar, em inglês simples, sobre decisões difíceis e riscos, mostrando segurança diante de um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
Making decisions with incomplete information is part of a senior executive's daily life. In large projects, you don't always have all the data, and even so you have to decide. The key terms here are decision, risk and to choose. Talking about this in simple English shows the client that you think clearly, even under pressure.

At Racional, decisions like these appear at every phase of the viability → engineering → pre-construction → build model. In a hyperscale data center for a client such as Amazon or Google, for example, you have to weigh deadlines, costs and risks before moving forward. The North American client values those who take the decision responsibly and explain the options in an honest way.

This lesson gives you the words to compare options, talk about risks, and say that you decided carefully. You will learn to use short sentences like "We have two options" and "We need to manage the risk". No rare terms: the focus is on sounding confident and clear when making a decision.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar frases simples: "We have two options.", "There is a risk here." e "I made a decision."

Com poucas palavras você consegue explicar uma escolha difícil ao cliente.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião, há um risco no prazo da obra. O cliente norte-americano quer saber como você vai decidir. Você explica as opções e a sua escolha.
lessons.context: We have two options here. Both have a risk. Option one is faster, but it costs more. Option two is safer. I made a decision. We will choose option two. We need to manage the risk with care.

vocab.example: It was a hard decision.
We need to decide today.
We will choose option two.
We have two options.
There is a risk here.
Option two is safer.
Let's compare the options.
We manage the risk with care.
We are ready to move forward.
We are careful with money.
The cost is high.
Option one is fast.
I am not sure yet.
I need to think it over.

exercises.title: 1. Termos de decisão
exercises.explanation: São as palavras-base para falar de escolhas difíceis em inglês.

exercises.title: 2. Explique uma escolha
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 a 3 frases simples comparando duas opções de uma obra. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês da aula (por exemplo option, risk, to choose, safe).
exercises.modelAnswer: We have two options. Option one is fast, but it has a risk. Option two is safer, so we will choose it.
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos da aula.

exercises.title: 3. A escolha mais segura
exercises.prompt: Para descrever a opção com menos perigo, você diz que ela é:

options.text: safer
louder
options.whyWrong: 'Louder' é mais barulhento, não tem a ver com risco.

options.text: older
options.whyWrong: 'Older' é mais velho; aqui falamos de segurança, não de idade.

exercises.explanation: 'Safer' = mais seguro, com menos risco. É a palavra certa para essa comparação.

exercises.title: 4. Monte a frase
exercises.explanation: Ordem simples: We + have + two + options.

exercises.title: 5. Anuncie a decisão em voz alta
exercises.targetText: We have two options. I made a decision. We choose the safe one.
exercises.translation: Temos duas opções. Eu tomei uma decisão. Escolhemos a opção segura.
exercises.prompt: Fale como se estivesse fechando o assunto numa reunião com o cliente.
exercises.explanation: Anunciar a decisão com clareza passa firmeza ao cliente.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por uns 15 a 20 segundos, explique duas opções para uma obra, diga qual é o risco de cada uma e qual você escolhe.
takeaways: I can compare two options in simple English.
I can talk about a risk.
I can announce a decision.
I can say we are ready to move forward.

lessons.title: KPIs, OKRs & performance metrics
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue falar, em inglês simples, sobre metas e resultados (KPIs) da Racional diante de um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
Goals and indicators show, with numbers, whether a project is going well. In business English, this comes up as KPI (key performance indicator), target and results. North American clients like clear data: they want to know whether the project is on schedule, on budget and at the agreed quality.

At Racional, with 620+ projects delivered, talking about numbers is talking about credibility. In projects of 18 to 24 months for clients such as Microsoft, Amazon and Google, every milestone has a target. Knowing how to say, in simple English, that the company is on track or that it will hit the target conveys control and confidence.

This lesson gives you the words to present results without overcomplicating. You will learn how to say that a goal was met, that a number is within plan, and that the team will deliver results. The focus is clarity: numbers speak for themselves, and your English just needs to be direct.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar frases simples: "We are on track.", "We hit the target." e "The results are good."

Com essas frases você apresenta números de forma clara e segura.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião de acompanhamento, o cliente norte-americano quer saber os números do projeto. Você apresenta as metas e os resultados.
lessons.context: Let me show the numbers. We are on track. We hit the target this month. The results are good. One number is behind the plan, but we have a plan to fix it. The team will deliver results.

vocab.example: This KPI looks good.
We hit the target.
This metric is important.
The results are good.
We hit the target this month.
We missed the target last month.
The project is on track.
One number is behind the plan.
The team will deliver.
We reached a milestone.
Our goal is clear.
This number is high.
We track the numbers every week.
The performance is strong.

exercises.title: 1. Bater a meta
exercises.prompt: Quando o time alcança o número combinado, em inglês você diz:

options.text: We hit the target.
We lost the target.
options.whyWrong: 'We lost' não é a expressão usada; para alcançar dizemos 'hit'.

options.text: We eat the target.
options.whyWrong: 'Eat' é comer; aqui o verbo certo é 'hit' (bater/alcançar).

exercises.explanation: 'To hit the target' = bater a meta, alcançar o número planejado.

exercises.title: 2. Termos de metas e resultados
exercises.explanation: São as palavras centrais para apresentar números a um cliente.

exercises.title: 3. Ouça e escreva
exercises.correctText: We are on track and we hit the target.
exercises.explanation: Frase curta e positiva para abrir uma reunião de resultados.

exercises.title: 4. Apresente os números
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 a 3 frases simples apresentando o andamento de uma obra. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês da aula (por exemplo target, on track, results, to deliver).
exercises.modelAnswer: The project is on track. We hit the target this month. The results are good and the team will deliver.
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos da aula.

exercises.title: 5. Resuma os resultados em voz alta
exercises.targetText: We are on track. We hit the target. The results are good.
exercises.translation: Estamos no caminho certo. Batemos a meta. Os resultados são bons.
exercises.prompt: Fale como se abrisse a parte de números da reunião com o cliente.
exercises.explanation: Comece pelo positivo e fale com calma; os números fazem o resto.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por uns 15 a 20 segundos, apresente o andamento de uma obra: diga se está on track, se bateu a meta e o que o time vai entregar.
takeaways: I can present results in simple English.
I can say we hit the target.
I can say the project is on track.
I can talk about a metric or a number.

lessons.title: US business culture: directness, time, formality
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você entende e usa, em inglês simples, hábitos da cultura de negócios norte-americana — ser direto, pontual e profissional.
lessons.overview:
The business culture of the United States has striking traits: people are direct, they value punctuality, and they like to get to the point. Understanding this helps you build a real connection with the client, and not just exchange information. Since most of Racional's clients are North American, this cultural repertoire makes a difference in every conversation.

In practice, this shows up in simple things. Arriving on time shows respect. A firm handshake and addressing the person by their first name (first-name basis) create closeness. At the same time, Americans like to keep the tone professional and to receive clear answers. Being aware of this avoids misunderstandings in long projects, lasting 18 to 24 months, with key accounts such as Microsoft, Amazon and Google.

This is a bridge lesson, lighter and more conversational. The focus is genuine connection, not heavy grammar. You will learn short phrases to break the ice, show respect for the other person's time, and sound warm and direct at the same time — exactly what the North American client expects.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar frases simples: "Let me get to the point.", "Thank you for your time." e "It is nice to meet you."

São frases que mostram respeito e abrem uma conversa de forma calorosa.
lessons.situation: Você encontra um cliente norte-americano pela primeira vez. Você quebra o gelo, mostra respeito pelo tempo dele e vai direto ao ponto.
lessons.context: It is nice to meet you. Thank you for your time. I will be direct. Let me get to the point. In the US, people like to be on time. They like clear answers. I value your time, so I will keep it short.

lessons.title: Board meetings & shareholder communication
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue conduzir, em inglês simples, partes de uma reunião de conselho e falar com acionistas e stakeholders.
lessons.overview:
Board meetings and communication with shareholders require clarity and calm. The key terms here are board meeting, shareholder and stakeholder. As a member of Racional's Executive Board, you need to open a meeting, present the main point, and answer questions with confidence — and all of this, often, in English.

At Racional, with more than 50 years and large-scale projects, governance and transparency are part of the company's reputation. When presenting the quarterly results or reassuring a stakeholder about the deadline of a project for Microsoft, Amazon or Google, your English needs to be direct and reliable, with no beating around the bush.

This lesson gives you simple phrases to lead these moments. You will learn how to open a meeting, state what the main point is, reassure those who are concerned, and open the floor to questions. The goal is to sound clear and confident, even before a demanding board.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar frases simples: "Let me start with the headline.", "That is a fair point." e "I am happy to take questions."

Essas frases ajudam você a conduzir uma reunião com calma e clareza.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião de conselho, você apresenta os resultados do trimestre. Um stakeholder norte-americano faz uma pergunta sobre o prazo. Você responde com calma.
lessons.context: Thank you all for coming. Let me start with the headline. The quarterly results are good. The project is on track. I know there is a concern about the timeline. That is a fair point. We have a plan, and I want to reassure you. I am happy to take questions now.

lessons.title: Risk management & contingency planning
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá falar sobre riscos de uma obra e planos de contingência usando frases simples em inglês com clientes norte-americanos.
lessons.overview:
Risk management is one of the most strategic topics in the daily life of a senior construction executive. At Racional, every large project, such as a data center for Microsoft or Amazon, brings risks of schedule, cost and safety. Knowing how to talk about risk management in English shows the client that the company has control and maturity.

A North American client values directness. They want to hear, clearly, what the worst-case scenario is and what the contingency plan is. In projects of 18 to 24 months, supplier delays or scope changes are common, and the executive needs to explain how Racional will mitigate each risk before it turns into a problem.

In this lesson you will learn how to identify a risk, describe its impact, and present a safeguard. These are short, confident sentences for governance meetings, where the client expects to hear a leader who sees risk early and acts with calm and a defined plan.
lessons.intro:
Vamos usar três estruturas-âncora: "We see a risk in..." (Vemos um risco em...), "Our plan is to..." (Nosso plano é...) e "If that happens, we will..." (Se isso acontecer, nós vamos...).

Pratique também o verbo to mitigate (reduzir/mitigar) e a expressão contingency plan (plano de contingência).
lessons.situation: Em uma reunião de governança, um cliente norte-americano pergunta a Cássio quais são os principais riscos da obra de um data center e como a Racional vai lidar com eles.
lessons.context: Every project has risks. On a big build, the main risks are time, cost and safety. Our team finds each risk early. We look at the impact and how likely it is. Then we make a plan. For each risk, we have a backup plan. If a supplier is late, we have a second supplier. We keep a safety buffer in the budget. We talk to the client about every risk. We want no surprises. A good plan keeps the project on track.

vocab.example: Risk management is part of every project.
We have a contingency plan for delays.
We identify a risk early.
This risk has a small impact.
The likelihood of a delay is low.
We mitigate the risk with a buffer.
Our cost exposure is low this month.
The worst-case scenario is a two-week delay.
We keep a safety buffer in the budget.
Our fallback is a second supplier.
We use early warning signs to act fast.
A supply delay can stop the work.
I flag a risk as soon as I see it.

lessons.title: M&A, joint ventures & strategic partnerships
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá falar sobre parcerias, joint ventures e fusões com frases simples, mostrando o valor de unir forças com um cliente.
lessons.overview:
Growth through partnerships is a central topic on a senior executive's agenda. Racional, with more than 50 years and 620 projects, sometimes joins forces with other companies in a joint venture or in a strategic partnership to deliver large-scale projects, such as a shopping center or a hyperscale data center.

When the client is North American, they want to understand the logic of the deal: the strategic rationale and the synergy that each side brings. Talking about this in simple English helps the executive show that Racional knows how to choose partners, share risk, and create value in a clear and mature way.

In this lesson you will learn how to explain why a partnership makes sense, what each side brings to the table, and how the two companies grow together. These are direct sentences, useful for strategic conversations and for the start of the commercial cycle of a large project.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar três estruturas-âncora: "We bring X to the table" (Trazemos X para a mesa), "Together we can..." (Juntos podemos...) e "We share the risk" (Dividimos o risco).

Lembre também das palavras joint venture (empreendimento conjunto) e synergy (sinergia).
lessons.situation: Cássio conversa com um cliente norte-americano sobre uma possível joint venture para construir e operar um grande shopping center juntos.
lessons.context: Sometimes two companies work better together. This is a partnership. In a joint venture, two firms build one project as a team. Each side brings something to the table. We bring local experience and a strong team. The partner brings money and market access. We share the risk and the cost. We also share the value. The goal is simple. Together we can do more than alone. A good partner makes the project stronger.

vocab.example: A merger joins two companies into one.
An acquisition is when one firm buys another.
We start a joint venture for the mall.
This is a strategic partnership for both sides.
The strategic rationale is clear and simple.

Both companies share the risk.
We do due diligence before the deal.

lessons.title: Succession planning & talent management
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá falar sobre sucessão e desenvolvimento de talentos, mostrando ao cliente que a Racional tem um time forte e preparado.
lessons.overview:
A North American client who signs an 18 to 24 month contract wants to know whether the company will have prepared leaders throughout the entire project. That is why succession planning and talent management are strategic topics for a senior executive at Racional.

With 620 projects and 50 years of history, Racional has built a strong talent pipeline. Knowing how to explain, in simple English, how the company develops and retains its professionals reassures the client: the project does not depend on a single person.

In this lesson you will learn how to talk about the leadership team, how the company prepares successors, and how it keeps knowledge in-house. These are useful sentences for governance meetings and for building long-term trust with key accounts such as Microsoft, Amazon and Google.
lessons.intro:
Vamos usar três estruturas-âncora: "We have a strong team" (Temos um time forte), "We develop our people" (Desenvolvemos nossa gente) e "We promote from within" (Promovemos de dentro).

Lembre das palavras successor (sucessor) e to retain (reter).
lessons.situation: Em uma reunião de governança, um cliente norte-americano pergunta a Cássio como a Racional garante liderança forte durante todo o projeto de 24 meses.
lessons.context: A long project needs strong leaders. We plan for this. We call it succession planning. We have a deep team, not just one person. We find key talent early. We develop our people every year. We mentor them. We promote from within. When a leader moves up, a successor is ready. This keeps the project safe. We also keep good people. We retain our best talent. A strong team is a strong promise to the client.

vocab.example: Succession planning keeps the team ready.
We have a strong talent pipeline.
We retain our best people.
Our retention is high this year.
We find key talent early.
We develop our people every year.
Senior leaders mentor young engineers.
A successor is ready for each role.
Continuity keeps the project safe.
We promote from within the company.
We support our high-potential people.
We onboard new leaders fast.
Knowledge transfer keeps the team strong.

lessons.title: Small talk & conversation starters
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá iniciar e manter uma conversa leve (small talk) com um cliente norte-americano antes de uma reunião.
lessons.overview:
Before every formal meeting there are a few minutes of light conversation, the small talk. For a senior executive at Racional, those minutes are worth gold: they are what create the human bond with a North American client over the 18 to 24 month cycle of a project.

The US business culture likes a quick and friendly small talk: asking about the trip, the weekend or the weather. Knowing how to break the ice with natural phrases makes the executive seem close and confident, even with simple English.

In this lighter lesson, the focus is genuine connection, not grammar. You will learn short and warm questions to welcome a client who has just arrived in São Paulo to visit a Racional project, such as a data center or a shopping center.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar três aberturas naturais: "How was your trip?" (Como foi sua viagem?), "How's everything on your end?" (Como vão as coisas por aí?) e "Let's grab a coffee" (Vamos tomar um café).

Lembre da ideia de to break the ice (quebrar o gelo).
lessons.situation: Um cliente norte-americano acaba de chegar a São Paulo para visitar uma obra. Cássio o recebe com uma conversa leve antes da reunião.
lessons.context: It is good to start with small talk. Just a few friendly minutes. You can ask about the trip. "How was your trip?" You can ask about the weekend. People like easy questions. You break the ice. Then everyone feels relaxed. After a long flight, jet lag is normal. So keep it simple and warm. "Let's grab a coffee first." Small talk builds trust. Trust helps the long project.

vocab.example: Small talk helps people relax.
How was your trip to São Paulo?
When did you fly in?

vocab.pt: Como vão as coisas por aí?
vocab.example: How's everything on your end this week?
It's nice to catch up.
A simple question can break the ice.
Hi, how's it going?
Let's grab a coffee first.
Any weekend plans?

lessons.title: Crisis communication & reputation
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá comunicar uma má notícia ou um problema na obra de forma transparente, assumindo responsabilidade e reassegurando o cliente.
lessons.overview:
In long projects, problems happen: a delay, an unexpected technical issue, an incident. What defines a great executive is the way they communicate it. Crisis communication and reputation are strategic topics for Racional's leadership, which protects the brand built over 50 years.

The North American client values transparency and directness. They want to hear the executive take ownership, explain the root cause, and show the corrective action. Hiding the problem destroys trust; admitting it with a plan strengthens it.

In this lesson you will learn how to deliver difficult news with calm: acknowledge the problem, be direct, reassure the client, and promise to keep them informed. These are short, confident sentences for a delicate moment in a large project, such as a data center or hospital.
lessons.intro:
Vamos usar três estruturas-âncora: "Let me be straight with you" (Deixe-me ser direto), "We take ownership of this" (Assumimos a responsabilidade) e "We will get back on track" (Vamos voltar aos trilhos).

Lembre de to keep you posted (mantê-lo informado) e root cause (causa raiz).
lessons.situation: Há um atraso em uma obra da Racional. Cássio liga para o cliente norte-americano para comunicar o problema e o plano de correção.
lessons.context: Bad news is hard, but we share it fast. We are honest. "Let me be straight with you. We have a delay." First, we take ownership. The problem is ours to fix. Then we explain the root cause. After that, we share the corrective action. We tell the client the plan. "We will get back on track." We also reassure them. "We will keep you posted." Clear and honest words protect trust and our reputation.

vocab.example: Crisis communication must be clear and fast.

We had a small setback this week.

We will get back on track soon.

Accountability builds trust.

lessons.title: Corporate governance & compliance
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá falar sobre governança e compliance, mostrando ao cliente que a Racional segue regras claras, auditorias e um código de conduta.
lessons.overview:
Governance and compliance are pillars of trust in any large contract. For North American clients such as Microsoft, Amazon and Google, corporate governance and compliance are not details: they are requirements. Racional, with 50 years and 620 projects, sustains its reputation precisely on clear rules.

A senior executive needs to explain, in simple English, how the company works: the board, the internal controls, the audits and the code of conduct. Showing that Racional is compliant and transparent reduces the risk perceived by the client and speeds up the decision.

In this lesson you will learn how to describe the governance structure and the commitment to rules and ethics. These are direct sentences, useful in meetings with the client's compliance and legal areas, common at the start of large projects such as data centers.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar três estruturas-âncora: "We are fully compliant" (Estamos totalmente em conformidade), "We follow a code of conduct" (Seguimos um código de conduta) e "We are audited every year" (Somos auditados todo ano).

Lembre de board (conselho) e oversight (supervisão).
lessons.situation: A área de compliance do cliente norte-americano pede a Cássio uma explicação sobre a governança da Racional antes de assinar o contrato.
lessons.context: Big clients care about rules. They want a clear and honest company. We follow strong corporate governance. We have a board that gives oversight. We have internal controls for every project. We are compliant with the law and the regulations. We are audited every year. We follow a code of conduct. Everyone is accountable. We are transparent with the client. Clear rules and ethics build long-term trust.

vocab.example: We follow strong corporate governance.
Compliance is part of every project.
The board gives oversight.
We have internal controls for each step.
We are fully compliant with the law.
We follow every regulation.
An audit checks our numbers.
We are audited every year.
The board provides oversight.
Everyone here is accountable.
We follow a clear code of conduct.
The board must approve big decisions.
We are transparent with the client.
Ethics guide all our work.

lessons.title: ESG & sustainability na construção
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você falará, em inglês simples, sobre as práticas de sustentabilidade e ESG da Racional em uma conversa com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
For Racional's North American clients — such as Microsoft, Amazon and Google —, sustainability has stopped being a differentiator and has become a requirement. When a client decides to build a hyperscale data center or a large headquarters, they ask about carbon footprint, energy efficiency and green certification already in the first meeting.

As a board executive, you need to show that Racional has a clear ESG agenda: use of renewable energy, waste management and responsible sourcing of materials. Over more than 50 years and 620 projects, the company has also built its reputation by reducing the environmental impact of each project.

In this lesson you will learn how to say, in a short and direct way, that Racional is committed to net zero targets and that it takes care of the community impact. This vocabulary positions you as a serious partner in front of a demanding American client.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar três frases-âncora: "We are committed to net zero by 2050.", "We use renewable energy on our sites." e "We reduce the environmental impact of every project."

Lembre-se: to be committed to sempre vem seguido de um substantivo ou de verbo com -ing.
lessons.situation: Em uma reunião em São Paulo, um diretor da Microsoft pergunta como a Racional trata a sustentabilidade no projeto de um novo data center.
lessons.context: Sustainability is very important for us. We are committed to net zero. We use renewable energy on our sites. We manage waste and we recycle materials. Our goal is a low-carbon project. We also care about the local community. Safety comes first on every site. This is how we work.

lessons.title: Innovation & digital transformation
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreverá, em inglês simples, como a Racional usa tecnologia e dados para dar mais previsibilidade às obras.
lessons.overview:
Racional's technology clients live on innovation and digital transformation. When Microsoft or Amazon hire a construction company, they want to know whether the project will be run with modern, data-driven methods, and not with loose spreadsheets and decisions made in the dark.

Racional uses BIM (building information modeling) to plan each project and dashboards to give the client real-time visibility. This helps to track progress and to streamline the workflow of large projects, such as hyperscale data centers.

In this lesson you will learn how to talk about this area in a short and clear way: how the company uses cutting-edge technology to offer delivery certainty from the moment it breaks ground. For the Racional executive, this vocabulary shows the American client that the company thinks like a technology company, and not only a concrete one.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora desta aula: "We use BIM on every project.", "Our dashboard gives you real-time visibility." e "We track progress every day."

Repare que usamos o presente simples para falar de hábitos e processos da empresa.

lessons.title: Regional differences (NE, South, Midwest, West Coast)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conversará, em inglês simples, sobre as diferentes regiões dos Estados Unidos com um cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
Racional's clients live in very different regions of the States (the United States). A client from the West Coast, in Seattle or California, tends to be more laid-back; whereas someone from New York, on the East Coast, tends to be more fast-paced and direct.

Knowing how to talk about the Midwest and the South creates connection. In the South, people are known for their hospitality and even use y'all (an informal way of saying "you all"). Asking about someone's hometown or about the local food scene is a great way to break the ice.

This is a relationship lesson. For the Racional executive, who works with North American clients on projects of 18 to 24 months, light conversation about regions helps the client feel at home. The goal here is not heavy grammar, but a genuine and human connection.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "Where are you from in the States?", "People in the South are very friendly." e "I love the food scene there."

São frases simples para usar no início de uma conversa, antes da reunião de negócios.
lessons.situation: Antes de uma reunião, você conversa com um cliente do Google e descobre que ele é do Texas, no Sul dos EUA.
lessons.context: The United States is very big. The East Coast is fast-paced. The West Coast is more laid-back. People in the South are warm and friendly. The Midwest is calm and down-to-earth. Each place has a great food scene. I always ask people about their hometown. It makes them feel at home.

lessons.title: Change management
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explicará, em inglês simples, como a Racional conduz mudanças em um projeto e ganha o apoio do cliente.
lessons.overview:
In projects of 18 to 24 months, changes are normal: the client revises the scope, a new technology appears, or a deadline shifts. Change management is the way Racional handles these changes without losing control of the project and without losing the client's trust.

The secret is to get people's buy-in. When you explain the rationale for a change and use a phased approach, you reduce resistance and pushback. Keeping everyone in the loop helps to ease the transition.

For an American client, who values clarity and frankness, knowing how to communicate changes calmly is a sign of maturity. In this lesson you will learn how to say, in short sentences, that Racional will address concerns and ensure a smooth transition at every stage of the project.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "We will roll out the change in phases.", "I want to explain the rationale." e "We will keep everyone in the loop."

Note o uso de will para falar de planos e do que a empresa vai fazer.
lessons.situation: O cliente da Microsoft pede uma mudança no escopo da obra e você explica como a Racional vai conduzir essa mudança.
lessons.context: Change is normal in a long project. We manage change with care. First, I explain the rationale. Then we roll out the change in phases. We keep everyone in the loop. This way we reduce resistance. Our goal is a smooth transition for the whole team.

lessons.title: Stakeholder mapping & influence
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você falará, em inglês simples, sobre como identificar e engajar as pessoas-chave de um cliente.
lessons.overview:
In a large Racional project, there are many people involved. Knowing who the decision-maker is, who the influencer is, and who the gatekeeper is (the person who controls access) is essential. This work of mapping the stakeholders helps you know who to talk to and when.

Each person has a level of power and of interest in the project. The Racional executive needs to engage these people, align on objectives, and keep them informed. When you win over a champion (an internal advocate), it becomes easier to gain the buy-in of the whole client.

For American clients, who often have a decision committee and several approval levels, this mapping is decisive. In this lesson you will learn how to say, in short sentences, that Racional knows how to win over the right people and find a common ground with each of them.

Frases-âncora: "We map all the stakeholders.", "Who is the decision-maker?" e "We want to find common ground."

lessons.title: Executive presence & gravitas em inglês
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usará, em inglês simples, frases curtas e firmes para se posicionar com mais presença executiva.
lessons.overview:
Executive presence is the way you show up and speak in front of an important client. It is not about using difficult words in English; it is about being concise, composed and credible. For the Racional executive, this means conveying gravitas even in simple sentences.

In English, you don't need to speak fast. Learning to pause and to use phrases such as "My view is..." and "Let me be clear." helps you project confidence and come across as assured. When the client asks a difficult question, you can say "That's a fair question" and hold the line calmly.

With American clients, who value objectivity, this style is very effective. In this lesson you practice short sentences that show that Racional will not cut corners and that you know how to stand firm without losing your composure. Pause and clarity are worth more than many words.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "My view is clear.", "Let me be clear." e "That's a fair question."

Use pausas curtas entre as frases; isso ajuda a transmitir confiança.
lessons.situation: Em uma reunião tensa, um cliente da Amazon questiona o prazo da obra e você precisa responder com calma e firmeza.
lessons.context: Executive presence is about being calm and clear. I speak slowly. I pause. I keep my answers short. When a question is hard, I say: that's a fair question. My view is clear. We will not cut corners. I stand firm, but I stay polite.

lessons.title: Storytelling de liderança
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue contar uma história curta de liderança em inglês — situação, desafio, virada e lição — para inspirar uma equipe ou um cliente.
lessons.overview:
Leaders don't convince with numbers alone; they convince with stories. Leadership storytelling is the art of telling a real case in a simple way: what happened, what the challenge was, what the turning point was, and what the lesson learned was. For a member of the Executive Board, this skill turns a cold report into a message that stays in people's minds.

In Racional's routine, you live stories like these all the time. Think of a project delivered against the odds, a hyperscale data center for Microsoft or Amazon that had to be ready on time even with unexpected events. When you tell this case to a North American client, you show more than technical competence: you show character, resilience, and the company's culture of more than 50 years and 620 projects.

The secret is the structure, not the difficult words. You open with a sentence to set the scene, present the problem, show the turning point, and close with the takeaway. In this lesson you build this script in simple English, with short sentences that any American executive understands and that make your message resonate.
lessons.intro:
Vamos relembrar três frases-âncora que sustentam qualquer história de liderança: "Here's what happened..." (para abrir), "Halfway through, we had a problem." (para o desafio) e "In the end, we delivered on time." (para o fechamento).

A ideia é simples: situar, mostrar o desafio, contar a virada e terminar com a lição. Frases curtas, no presente e no passado simples.
lessons.situation: Num jantar com um cliente norte-americano, ele pergunta sobre o projeto mais difícil da Racional. Você conta, em inglês simples, a história de uma obra entregue no prazo contra todas as probabilidades.
lessons.context: Here's what happened. We had a big project for a client. The deadline was very tight. Halfway through, we found a problem on site. It was hard, but the team did not give up. In the end, we delivered on time. The lesson was simple: a strong team can do great things together.

vocab.example: Good storytelling helps people remember your message.
First, I set the scene for the team.
The deadline was our biggest challenge.
That meeting was the turning point.

lessons.title: Business dinners: etiquette & ordering
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue se comportar bem num jantar de negócios em inglês — receber ou ser recebido, pedir do cardápio e conversar de forma leve.
lessons.overview:
Much of the long-term relationship with international clients happens outside the meeting room. A business dinner is a strategic moment: it is where trust is born. Knowing how to host as a host or be a good guest shows respect for the other person's culture — something highly valued by North American executives.

For Racional, with projects of 18 to 24 months and long-term relationships with key accounts such as Microsoft, Amazon and Google, these dinners recur throughout the entire cycle. You don't need difficult English: you need simple and polite phrases to order a starter and a main course, ask the waiter for a recommendation, and make a bit of small talk.

The American business culture values human warmth with calibrated formality. Offering "It's on me" or a "Cheers" at the right moment builds rapport. In this lesson you will learn the key phrases of table etiquette, so you can move naturally between the professional and personal registers.
lessons.intro:
Três frases-âncora para a mesa: "I'll have the salmon, please." (para pedir), "What do you recommend?" (para pedir uma sugestão) e "It's on me." (para oferecer pagar).

Tom leve e educado: o objetivo é conexão, não gramática perfeita.

lessons.title: Chairing meetings as host
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue conduzir uma reunião em inglês como anfitrião — abrir, seguir a pauta, gerir o tempo e fechar com os próximos passos.
lessons.overview:
Running a meeting is to chair a meeting — and it is one of the most visible skills of an executive. When you are the host, it is up to you to open it, follow the agenda, keep the focus, and close with clarity. This makes all the difference, especially with North American clients, who value punctuality and getting straight to the point.

At Racional, the monthly and biweekly meetings with clients, the war rooms, and the project committees are the heart of the operation. In a data center for Amazon or in a hospital, it is in one of these meetings that scope, deadline, and risk are decided. Running them well in English means to stay on track, respect everyone's time, and leave with clear action items.

A good chair uses simple, firm phrases: "Let's get started", "Over to you", and "Let's wrap up". You don't need sophisticated English — you need clarity. In this lesson you will build that script for running a meeting, from the opening to the closing with next steps.
lessons.intro:
Três frases-âncora para conduzir: "Let's get started." (abrir), "Let's stay on track." (manter o foco) e "Let's wrap up with the next steps." (fechar).

Frases curtas e diretas, no presente. Você é quem dá o ritmo da reunião.
lessons.situation: Você preside a reunião mensal de obra com o cliente norte-americano de um data center. Abre a reunião, segue a pauta e fecha com os próximos passos.
lessons.context: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. Here is the agenda for today. First, the schedule. Then, the budget. In the interest of time, let's stay on track. Carlos, over to you. Now let's move on. To recap, we have two action items. Let's wrap up. I will follow up by email.

lessons.title: Public speaking — keynotes e town halls
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue estruturar uma fala curta para um keynote ou town hall em inglês — abrir com uma mensagem-chave e fechar com um pedido claro.
lessons.overview:
Public speaking is part of a senior executive's identity. A keynote at an industry event or a town hall with employees demands a clear message and a few well-chosen words. The goal is not to impress with vocabulary; it is to get the idea across.

For Racional — a construction company with more than 50 years of history, present in hyperscale data centers, hospitals, and shopping centers — the voice of the leadership matters. In a town hall, you inspire the team around the company's vision. In a keynote for North American clients and partners, you position the brand. In both, one simple key message is worth more than ten crowded slides.

Structure is what makes the talk work: you decide what to open with, which call to action to leave behind, and how to wrap up in a way that will make it stick. In this lesson you practice short, strong phrases to take the stage with ease.
lessons.intro:
Três frases-âncora para o palco: "I want to open with one idea." (abrir), "My key message is simple." (mensagem central) e "Here is what I ask of you." (chamado à ação).

Poucas palavras, ditas com calma. Uma mensagem clara fica na memória.
lessons.situation: Você sobe ao palco de um town hall da Racional para inspirar a equipe sobre o próximo ano. Abre com uma ideia, dá a mensagem-chave e fecha com um pedido claro.
lessons.context: Good morning, team. I want to open with one idea. We build the future. My key message is simple: we grow when we work as one team. This year was hard, but we are strong. Here is what I ask of you: stay focused and help each other. Thank you.

lessons.title: Sales pipeline & funnel review
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue revisar o funil de vendas em inglês — falar de oportunidades, estágios, probabilidade de fechar e próximos passos.
lessons.overview:
Every sale follows a path, and that path has a name: pipeline or funnel. Each deal starts as a lead, becomes a prospect, moves through stages, and finally becomes a closed deal. Reviewing the funnel means checking where each opportunity stands and what is missing to move it forward.

At Racional, the commercial cycle of a project lasts 18 to 24 months, and you work in pre-sales together with the commercial team. Talking about the funnel in English with a North American client or partner — a Microsoft or a Google evaluating a new data center — requires clarity about the probability of closing and the next steps for each opportunity.

The vocabulary is direct and widely used in the US. You need to say when a deal will move forward, when it stalls, and what your win rate is. In this lesson you practice these simple phrases to run a funnel review with confidence.
lessons.intro:
Três frases-âncora para a revisão: "This deal is in the final stage.", "The probability of closing is high." e "The next step is a meeting."

Presente simples e frases curtas. O foco é onde está cada negócio e o que vem a seguir.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião de pré-venda com a área comercial, você revisa o funil de um grande projeto com um cliente norte-americano e define os próximos passos.
lessons.context: Let's review the pipeline. We have three deals this month. The first deal is in the final stage. The probability of closing is high. The second one is a new lead. We need to qualify it. The third deal stalled, so we must move it forward. Our win rate is good this year.

lessons.title: Forecasting & quota management
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue falar de previsão de vendas e metas em inglês — dizer se está no rumo, acima ou abaixo da meta e revisar números.
lessons.overview:
Predicting results is part of any commercial leader's job. A forecast is the estimate of how much the company will sell or deliver in a given period. The goal has two common names: target and quota. A good executive knows how to say, in a few words, whether they are on track, whether they will fall short, or exceed the goal.

For Racional, with long projects of 18 to 24 months and relationships with international key accounts, the forecast is strategic: it guides hiring, purchasing, and cash flow. In a conversation with the headquarters of a North American client or with your own leadership, you need to explain the gap between forecast and actual and which assumptions support the number.

The secret is to be clear and honest. Showing a conservative forecast, explaining the run rate, and saying when you need to revise the forecast builds trust — something American executives value greatly. In this lesson you practice these simple phrases for forecasting and goals.
lessons.intro:
Três frases-âncora para a previsão: "We are on track to hit the target.", "There is a small gap this month." e "We may need to revise the forecast."

Frases curtas e honestas. O foco é a meta, o ritmo e a diferença.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião com a liderança e o cliente norte-americano, você apresenta a previsão do trimestre e explica a diferença em relação à meta.
lessons.context: Let me share the forecast for this quarter. The target is high, but we are on track. Our run rate is good. There is a small gap of ten percent this month. I am conservative with this number. If sales fall short, we will revise the forecast next month.

lessons.title: American politics: parties, elections, Congress
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue conversar com naturalidade sobre política dos Estados Unidos com um cliente americano, usando frases simples e mantendo uma postura neutra.
lessons.overview:
Talking about politics with an American client is delicate, but unavoidable. At dinners, on flights, and during meeting breaks, the topic comes up — and being able to follow the conversation, without taking sides, shows range and respect. In the United States there are two main parties: the Democrats and the Republicans. Every two years there is an election, and every four years a president is elected. Understanding this basic structure already puts you on a different level of conversation.

For an executive in Racional's leadership, this background matters because most clients are North American — investors and contractors for hyperscale data centers like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. These 18- to 24-month projects create long relationships, and the relationship is also built in these informal moments. Knowing what Congress is, what the midterms are, and why certain states decide the election (the swing states) gives you something to talk about and a genuine connection.

The golden rule for a foreigner is simple: to stay neutral. You follow along, ask questions, show interest — but you do not defend one side. US politics is the host's topic; your role is that of a curious and polite observer. That way you build closeness without ever risking putting a key account in an awkward spot.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula de conexão, não de gramática. Você só precisa de frases curtas e calorosas para acompanhar a conversa.

Guarde três âncoras: "I try to follow American politics." (Eu tento acompanhar a política americana.), "There are two main parties." (Há dois partidos principais.) e "I like to stay neutral." (Eu gosto de me manter neutro.)
lessons.situation: Num jantar de negócios, um cliente americano comenta sobre as próximas eleições e pergunta o que você acha. Você acompanha a conversa com interesse, mas mantém a neutralidade.
lessons.context: I try to follow American politics from the outside. I know you have two main parties: the Democrats and the Republicans. There is always an election close. The midterms are coming soon, right? As a guest, I like to stay neutral. But I really want to hear how you see it.

lessons.title: Pricing strategy & margin discussions
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue responder a um pedido de desconto em inglês, defender a margem e oferecer uma troca em vez de simplesmente baixar o preço.
lessons.overview:
Discussing price with an American client is a natural part of the commercial cycle. US business culture is direct: the request for a discount comes early and without detours. Your role, as an executive in Racional's leadership, is neither to give in nor to fight — it is to explain the pricing strategy and show the value behind the number. A price is justified, not apologized for.

The key concept is margin: the difference between cost and final price. In a project of 18 to 24 months — a data center for Microsoft or a shopping center for an investor — the margin is what guarantees quality, deadline, and safety. That is why we use value-based pricing: the client pays for the certainty of delivery, not just for the square meter. When the client pushes, you can offer a trade-off: "if we reduce this, we adjust that."

The golden rule is to never cut the price without asking for something in return. You can adjust the scope — deliver less for less — but a discount with no give-back teaches the client to doubt the value. And in some cases, the strongest decision is to walk away when the number doesn't work. Defending the margin is defending the health of the entire project.
lessons.intro:
Aqui você pratica a defesa de margem com frases simples e firmes.

Guarde três âncoras: "Let me explain our pricing strategy." (Deixe-me explicar nossa estratégia de preço.), "There is little room on the margin." (Há pouco espaço na margem.) e "I can lower the price if we adjust the scope." (Posso baixar o preço se ajustarmos o escopo.)
lessons.situation: Numa reunião, um cliente americano pede um desconto na proposta de um data center. Você defende a margem e oferece uma troca em vez de simplesmente reduzir o preço.
lessons.context: Thank you for your offer. Let me explain our pricing strategy. The price reflects our quality and our on-time delivery. There is little room on the margin. But I want to help. I can lower the price if we adjust the scope. This is a fair trade-off for both of us.

lessons.title: Key account management
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue conduzir o relacionamento com uma key account em inglês — fazer o follow-up, antecipar necessidades e propor ampliar o escopo ao longo do projeto.
lessons.overview:
A signed contract is the beginning, not the end. A key account is worth more for the recurring business than for a single project. For Racional, with projects of 18 to 24 months, taking care of the client during and after delivery is what turns a one-off contract into a long-term partnership. And this is done, in large part, in English — directly with North American investors and contractors.

The central move is the follow-up: you reach out to the client, not the other way around. A regular check-in shows that Racional is present. Over time, you start to anticipate needs — offering the solution before the client asks. Because there is always a clear point of contact, the client knows whom to turn to, and that builds trust.

The long-term goal is repeat business: the next project, the renewal of the contract, the chance to expand the scope of an ongoing project. All of this depends on one simple and constant thing: to build trust, by delivering what was agreed and showing up before the problem, not after. That is how you retain a key account for years.

Aqui você pratica o cuidado proativo com o cliente, em frases simples.

Guarde três âncoras: "I wanted to check in on the project." (Eu queria fazer um contato sobre o projeto.), "We see a long-term partnership here." (Vemos uma parceria de longo prazo aqui.) e "There may be room to expand the scope." (Pode haver espaço para ampliar o escopo.)

lessons.title: RFPs, RFQs & proposal review
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você entende e usa em inglês os termos de uma RFP/RFQ, sabe falar de prazos e entregáveis e consegue confirmar que a proposta atende aos critérios do cliente.
lessons.overview:
Before any contract comes the formal selection process. The American client sends an RFP (Request for Proposal) or an RFQ (Request for Quotation), and Racional needs to respond with a clear, complete proposal. In large projects — a data center for Amazon, a shopping center for an investor — this document decides who gets into the game. Knowing how to read it and respond to it in English is part of the leadership's job.

Every RFP brings requirements, a scope of work, and a timeline. Your proposal needs to address each point and list the deliverables clearly. When the proposal covers everything that was asked for, it is compliant and meets the criteria. When an item is missing, the client may disqualify Racional from the process — which is why the care is total.

There is also the RFI (Request for Information), an earlier stage in which the client only wants to get to know the supplier. In every case, the golden rule is the same: to submit on time and respond exactly to what was asked. A winning proposal is not the prettiest; it is the one that meets each requirement in the clearest way and within the agreed bid.
lessons.intro:
Aqui você pratica a linguagem de propostas com frases simples.

Guarde três âncoras: "We will submit our proposal on time." (Vamos enviar nossa proposta no prazo.), "Our proposal meets all the requirements." (Nossa proposta atende a todos os requisitos.) e "Let me address each point." (Deixe-me responder a cada ponto.)
lessons.situation: Um cliente americano envia uma RFP para a construção de um shopping center. Você confirma o recebimento e garante que a Racional responderá a todos os requisitos no prazo.
lessons.context: Thank you for the RFP. We read all the requirements. Our team will address each point. The scope of work is clear, and we can meet the timeline. We will submit our proposal on time. Our proposal will meet all your criteria.

lessons.title: Contract structuring & terms
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue falar em inglês sobre os principais termos de um contrato — prazos de pagamento, garantia, multa e cláusulas — e alinhar pontos com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
When the proposal is accepted, the contract comes next. Structuring the terms clearly protects both sides and avoids conflict over the 18 to 24 months of a Racional project. Each clause defines a rule of the game: who pays what, when, and what happens if something fails. For an executive in the leadership, mastering this language in English is essential in negotiations with North American clients, who treat the contract with formality and attention to detail.

The central points are the payment terms, often tied to a milestone payment — the client pays as the project advances. There is also the warranty, the penalty for delay, and the liability of each party. In a data center or shopping center, these numbers are large, and every word of the contract carries weight.

The flow is simple: the parties need to align on the points, then sign off, and from there the contract is binding. If something changes, it is possible to amend the contract. The golden rule is to always honor a contract: in the North American world, the word given on paper is worth gold, and respecting it is what builds long-term trust.
lessons.intro:
Aqui você pratica os termos de contrato em frases simples e diretas.

Guarde três âncoras: "Let's align on the payment terms." (Vamos alinhar as condições de pagamento.), "The contract is binding for both sides." (O contrato é vinculante para os dois lados.) e "We always honor our contracts." (Nós sempre cumprimos nossos contratos.)
lessons.situation: Numa reunião com um cliente americano, você revisa o contrato de um shopping center e alinha os termos de pagamento, a garantia e a multa por atraso.
lessons.context: Let's go over the terms together. The payment terms are clear: we use milestone payments. Each clause protects both sides. We offer a warranty on our work. There is a penalty for any delay. We always honor our contracts.

lessons.title: Wine, food & restaurant English
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue conversar com naturalidade num jantar de negócios — pedir comida e vinho, fazer recomendações, brindar e oferecer-se para pagar a conta.
lessons.overview:
A large part of the relationship with an American client happens at the table. A business dinner is where the relationship cools down or warms up — and knowing how to move naturally between the menu and the conversation makes all the difference. For an executive in Racional's leadership, who hosts US investors and contractors over projects of 18 to 24 months, these dinners are as strategic as the formal meetings.

The vocabulary is simple and useful: the starter, the main course, the wine list. You can recommend a dish, suggest a full-bodied wine, or comment that something is outstanding. Knowing how to pair the wine with the food, or simply asking for a light bite, shows care for the guest and opens up conversation about the local cuisine.

The moment of the toast is special: raise your glass and say "Cheers!" or "Here's to a great project!" And, at the end, offering to pay — "It's on us." or "Let me get the check." — is a gesture of hospitality that the American client values. Small gestures like these, in simple English, build long-term trust.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula de conexão, não de gramática. Tom leve, frases curtas e calorosas.

Guarde três âncoras: "Can I recommend the main course?" (Posso recomendar o prato principal?), "Here's to a great project!" (Um brinde a um ótimo projeto!) e "It's on us." (É por nossa conta.)
lessons.situation: Você leva um cliente americano a um restaurante em São Paulo para um jantar de negócios e conduz o momento com hospitalidade, da escolha do prato ao pagamento da conta.
lessons.context: Welcome! Let me recommend a good starter. The main course here is outstanding. Would you like to see the wine list? This red is full-bodied. It pairs well with the meat. Let's toast. Here's to a great project! And tonight, it's on us.

lessons.title: Partnerships & channel management
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala sobre parcerias e gestão de canais em inglês — propondo, estruturando e cuidando de relações comerciais de longo prazo com clientes e parceiros norte-americanos.
lessons.overview:
A partnership is more than a contract: it is a relationship of trust built over time. At Racional, projects last 18 to 24 months, and the big clients — like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google — come back for new data centers and new projects. That is why thinking about a long-term partnership, and not a single sale, is a central part of the leadership's vision.

Managing this relationship well means making the roles and responsibilities clear, seeking a win-win agreement, and showing a good track record. When the client trusts Racional, it becomes the go-to partner and even generates a referral to new clients. For a North American executive, clarity and track record count for a lot: he wants to know whom he is talking to and what has already been delivered.

In this lesson, the focus is on aligning expectations and taking care of the account. You will learn to say that you want to align on priorities, to propose a shared roadmap, and to talk about to expand the account. These are simple phrases that help Cássio position himself as a strategic leader, not just a supplier.
lessons.intro:
Vamos usar três frases-âncora: "We want to be your go-to partner.", "Let's align on the next steps." e "Our track record speaks for itself."

Pratique cada uma em voz alta antes dos exercícios. São curtas e diretas, do jeito que o cliente norte-americano gosta.
lessons.situation: Em uma reunião de planejamento, Cássio conversa com um diretor da Microsoft sobre transformar uma obra pontual em uma parceria de longo prazo para vários data centers.
lessons.context: We want to be your go-to partner. Our track record is strong. We finished many projects on time and on budget. Let's align on a shared roadmap for the next two years. We can define clear roles and responsibilities. This is a win-win. You get a reliable partner, and we grow together.

lessons.title: Pre-sales: técnico + comercial em dupla
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você atua na pré-venda em dupla com a área comercial em inglês — somando sua autoridade técnica ao discurso comercial para convencer o cliente norte-americano antes da proposta.
lessons.overview:
The pre-sales phase happens before the formal proposal. It is the moment when the client wants to understand whether Racional can, in fact, deliver the project. Here, the commercial team and the technical team work as a pair: the commercial side handles the relationship and the value; the technical lead brings the confidence of engineering. For Cássio, from the leadership, this technical authority is worth gold — it is what gives credibility to the conversation.

A good executive knows when to bring in the specialist and when to hand over to the commercial side. He also knows how to walk someone through the solution and to address concerns from the client. In projects like data centers for Amazon or Google, the client wants to hear that the project is viable (feasibility) and predictable, with reduced risks (to de-risk).

The secret is to be in sync with the commercial area: the two voices tell the same story. In this lesson, you practice simple phrases to show that you understand the technical side and, at the same time, speak the business language of the North American client.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora desta aula: "Let me walk you through the plan.", "What this means for you is less risk." e "I'll hand over to our sales lead now."

São pontes entre o lado técnico e o comercial. Use-as para conduzir a conversa com calma.
lessons.situation: Em uma reunião de pré-venda com a Amazon, Cássio apresenta a parte técnica de um data center e depois passa a palavra para o diretor comercial.
lessons.context: Thank you for your time. Let me walk you through the plan. The project is feasible. We can build it on time. What this means for you is a predictable timeline and less risk. I will address your concerns about the budget now. Then I will hand over to our sales lead. We are in sync on every point.

lessons.title: Bid review & go/no-go decisions
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você participa de uma análise de proposta e de decisões go/no-go em inglês — pesando risco, margem e capacidade para decidir se a Racional deve concorrer a um projeto.
lessons.overview:
Before Racional enters a bid, the leadership runs an analysis of the proposal: the bid review. The central question is the go/no-go decision: is it worth it to bid on this project? It is a strategic decision that Cássio follows closely, because it involves risk, margin, and the company's name.

To decide, the team evaluates the fit with what Racional does best, the scope of the project, and the current execution capacity. It is also necessary to weigh the risk and look at the margin: a thin margin can be a red flag. In some cases, the best option is to walk away; in others, a conditional go is worthwhile.

In large projects, such as data centers for Google, a single deal-breaker can change everything. In this lesson, you practice how to say, in simple English, whether it is a "go" or a "no-go" and how to explain the trade-off behind the decision.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "It's a good fit for us.", "The margin is too thin." e "My vote is a conditional go."

Use "go" e "no-go" para deixar sua posição clara e direta.
lessons.situation: Em uma reunião interna, Cássio avalia com o time se a Racional deve concorrer a um data center da Google, pesando margem, escopo e capacidade.
lessons.context: Let's review this bid. Is it a good fit for us? The scope is clear, but the margin is thin. We need to weigh the risk and check our capacity. A thin margin is a red flag for me. My vote is a conditional go. We bid only if we get more time.
