lessons.title: Win/loss analysis
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz uma análise de ganhos e perdas (win/loss) em inglês — entendendo por que a Racional ganhou ou perdeu uma proposta e extraindo aprendizados para a próxima.
lessons.overview:
After each bid, the leadership runs a win/loss analysis. Winning or losing a project always brings a lesson. The question is simple: what decided the outcome? In English, this is what tipped the decision. For Cássio, this analysis is strategic: it shows where Racional is strong and where it needs to improve.

An important step is to ask the client for feedback and to take it on board. Sometimes the competitor offered a lower price; sometimes there was a shortcoming in the proposal. Each case becomes a lesson learned and helps you understand the deciding factor.

Even when Racional loses, it is important to keep the door open and to follow up with the client, because a new project may come up down the road. In this lesson, you practice how to run this to debrief in simple English, with North American clients who value frankness.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "What tipped the decision?", "Thank you for the feedback." e "Let's keep the door open."

Use-as para fechar a conversa de forma positiva, mesmo numa derrota.
lessons.situation: Após perder uma concorrência para um competidor, Cássio faz uma ligação com o cliente norte-americano para entender a decisão e manter a relação.
lessons.context: Thank you for your time. We did not win this bid. Can I ask what tipped the decision? Thank you for the feedback. We will take it on board. This is a good lesson learned for our team. Let's keep the door open. We can work together down the road.

lessons.title: US economy: Fed, inflation, interest rates
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você acompanha e comenta uma conversa sobre a economia dos EUA em inglês — Fed, inflação e juros — para se conectar com o cliente norte-americano em temas que ele acompanha de perto.
lessons.overview:
Racional's North American client follows the US economy closely. Three topics come up all the time in conversations: the Fed (the US central bank), inflation, and the interest rate. Being able to comment on these subjects, even with simple English, helps Cássio build a connection before the business meeting.

When inflation runs above target, the Fed may raise rates. When the economy starts to slow down, it may cut rates or keep rates steady. This affects the cost of capital and, as a result, the decisions to invest in new projects — something that matters a great deal to clients building data centers.

The goal here is not to become an economist, but to converse naturally. Phrases like from what I read and it seems like keep the tone light and cautious, without overstating. In this lesson, the focus is on genuine connection: showing interest in the client's world and keeping a pleasant conversation about the economy.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "From what I read, inflation is going down.", "It seems like the Fed will keep rates steady."

Use "from what I read" e "it seems like" para opinar sem soar como especialista.
lessons.situation: Antes de uma reunião, Cássio conversa de forma leve com um cliente norte-americano sobre a economia dos EUA e a decisão de juros do Fed.
lessons.context: From what I read, inflation is going down. It seems like the Fed will keep rates steady this month. The economy is slowing down a little. I think they want a soft landing. What do you think? Will they cut rates soon?

lessons.title: Customer success & retention
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz uma conversa de pós-venda focada em sucesso do cliente e retenção em inglês — garantindo a satisfação da key account e abrindo o próximo projeto.
lessons.overview:
The commercial cycle does not end with the delivery of the project. Next come customer success and retention: making sure the client stays satisfied and wants to come back. For Racional, with projects of 18 to 24 months and key accounts like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google, keeping a client is worth as much as winning a new one.

A proactive executive does not wait for the problem to appear. He does a check in frequently, seeks to get ahead of any pain point, and ensures the client will get full value from what was delivered. When the company delivers on what it promises (to deliver on a promise), the client becomes a loyal client.

This relationship opens doors: the chance to renew a contract, to offer an upsell, and to ask what's next. In this lesson, you practice how to do a simple and careful follow-up with the key account, in the direct and punctual way the North American client expects.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "I just want to check in.", "Are you happy with the result?" e "What's next for us?"

Use-as para manter o contato vivo e abrir o próximo projeto com naturalidade.
lessons.situation: Três meses após entregar um data center, Cássio liga para o cliente da Microsoft para confirmar a satisfação e falar sobre o próximo projeto.
lessons.context: Hello. I just want to check in with you. Are you happy with the result? We want you to get full value from this project. We are proactive. We try to get ahead of any problem. What's next for us? We would love to work with you again.

lessons.title: CRM e sales tech stack
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreve, em inglês simples, como a área comercial usa o CRM para acompanhar o funil de vendas e faz perguntas diretas sobre cada oportunidade.
lessons.overview:
Every construction company sells long projects, and at Racional a single contract can last 18 to 24 months. To avoid losing track of so many conversations, proposals, and decisions, the commercial area uses a CRM (client management system). It keeps every lead, every meeting, and every number in one place. As an executive director, you do not type anything into this system, but you need to read it and ask for results in English.

The center of it all is the pipeline: the list of open deals, each one at a stage. The dashboard shows this data in real time, and from it the company builds a forecast. When an American client from Microsoft, Amazon, or Google evaluates Racional for a data center, they want to see visibility and data, not long stories.

The secret is to talk about the funnel with numbers: stage, deal value, and close date. Three right words and your English already sounds senior. This lesson gives you that basic vocabulary to open a strategic conversation about the pipeline with North American clients.
lessons.intro:
Vamos fixar três estruturas-âncora simples: "We track every deal in our CRM." (Acompanhamos cada negócio no CRM), "This deal is in an early stage." (Este negócio está numa etapa inicial) e "My forecast is strong this quarter." (Minha previsão é forte neste trimestre).

Repare: presente simples e frases curtas. É assim que você fala de dados com naturalidade.
lessons.situation: Um cliente americano da Amazon avalia a Racional para um novo data center e pergunta como vocês acompanham as oportunidades comerciais. Você explica o uso do CRM.
lessons.context: We use a CRM to track every deal. The whole team sees the same pipeline in real time. The dashboard shows each opportunity and its stage. This gives me a clear forecast for the quarter. I can tell you the deal value and the close date for each one.

lessons.title: Cross-selling & upselling
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você propõe, em inglês simples, serviços adicionais a um cliente atual (cross-selling e upselling) ligando a oferta ao valor para ele.
lessons.overview:
Winning a new client is expensive. That is why selling more to those who already trust the company is one of the smartest ways to grow. In commercial language, this has two names: cross-selling (selling a different service to the same client) and upselling (selling a bigger or better version of what they already hired). For Racional, it is the natural path of a long-term relationship.

Think of a Microsoft client who hired Racional only for the construction of a data center. During the 18 to 24 months of the project, the chance comes up to also offer the pre-construction phase, the engineering, or a follow-on project. This is to expand the account and gain more wallet share. Each new service delivered well strengthens the trust and opens the next door.

The key point with American clients is to never sell just to sell. The offer needs to make sense for them. That is why we use gentle phrases like "it might make sense to..." and show how the extra service will add value. This lesson gives you the language to propose more without sounding aggressive.
lessons.intro:
Duas estruturas-âncora bem úteis: "It might make sense to add this service." (Talvez faça sentido adicionar este serviço) e "We can bring more value to your project." (Podemos agregar mais valor ao seu projeto).

São frases educadas, no presente simples, que abrem espaço sem pressionar o cliente.
lessons.situation: Um cliente da Microsoft contratou só a obra de um data center. Você vê a chance de oferecer também a fase de pré-construção e propõe isso com cuidado.
lessons.context: Your project is going well. I think it might make sense to add one more service. We can also lead the pre-construction phase for you. This is a tailored solution for your needs. It can add real value and save you time. We are happy to expand our work on this account.

lessons.title: Competitive intelligence
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explica, em inglês simples, por que a Racional é diferente da concorrência, destacando seus pontos fortes para um cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
In large projects, the client almost always compares several companies before deciding. Knowing how to talk about the competition without attacking anyone is an art. In business English, we call this looking at the competitive landscape and showing your differentiator: the thing only your company does so well.

Racional has strong arguments: 50+ years of history, 620+ projects delivered, and more than 10 million m² built. This is the track record that gives the client delivery certainty. Against global players, Racional's advantage is its local execution in Brazil: knowing the terrain, the suppliers, and the local rules. For a Google client about to build a data center, that is exactly what makes the company stand out.

With American clients, direct honesty pays off: "to be straight with you". You acknowledge where the competitors are good and show where we win. This lesson gives you the vocabulary to position Racional with confidence and without arrogance.
lessons.intro:
Estruturas-âncora desta aula: "Our track record is our main differentiator." (Nosso histórico é nosso principal diferencial) e "To be straight with you, this is where we win." (Para ser franco, é aqui que ganhamos).

Frases curtas, honestas e confiantes funcionam muito bem com clientes dos EUA.
lessons.situation: Um cliente da Google compara a Racional com duas construtoras globais. Ele pergunta, de forma direta, por que deveria escolher a Racional.
lessons.context: To be straight with you, we know our market well. Our track record is strong. We have built more than 620 projects in 50 years. This is our main differentiator. Global players are good, but our local execution is hard to match. This is where we win.

lessons.title: Family talk: spouse, kids, school
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conversa, em inglês simples, sobre a família de um cliente americano, fazendo perguntas naturais e respondendo sobre a sua.
lessons.overview:
Long-term business is done between people. Over the 18 to 24 months of a project, you will see the same American client many times, and not every conversation will be about the project. Talking about family is one of the simplest and warmest ways to build a long-term relationship. A sincere question like "How's the family?" often opens the meeting on a light note.

In this culture, the topic is safe and welcome: the client talks about their spouse, their kids, and their routine, like taking the children to school (to drop off at school). You do not need advanced English; you need human warmth and a few ready-made phrases. Showing genuine interest in the other person's life is worth more than any elegant sentence.

This is a bridge lesson: the goal is connection, not grammar. You will learn to ask, to answer with something of your own ("my oldest"; "the little one"), and to turn the question back with a simple "How about you?". Small exchanges like these, repeated throughout the project, build the trust that sustains a partnership.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora desta aula: "How's the family?" (Como está a família?), "My oldest is starting high school." (Meu mais velho vai começar o ensino médio) e "How about you?" (E você?).

Tom leve, presente simples, e sempre devolva a pergunta para manter a conversa viva.
lessons.situation: Antes de uma reunião, um cliente americano de longa data pergunta sobre a sua família. Você responde e devolve a pergunta com naturalidade.
lessons.context: It is good to see you again. How's the family? My oldest is starting high school this year. They grow up fast! The little one loves soccer. We try to juggle work and family every week. How about you? How are your kids?

lessons.title: Closing the deal: signing & handoff
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz, em inglês simples, o fechamento de um contrato e a passagem do projeto para a equipe de entrega de forma organizada.
lessons.overview:
After months of proposals and negotiation, the moment comes to close the deal and sign the contract. This is a delicate moment: the client wants to feel that the decision to move forward is safe. A simple, confident question like "Are we good to go?" confirms the agreement without beating around the bush.

But closing is not the end of your job. The next step is the handoff: introducing the project lead and the delivery team who will run the work. For an Amazon client about to build a data center with Racional, this transition needs to be seamless, with every process in place and a well-scheduled kickoff.

The biggest risk at this moment is letting something fall through the cracks. That is why the executive always closes by aligning the next steps and introducing the right people. This lesson gives you the language to finish the sale and start the delivery with confidence and clarity.
lessons.intro:
Estruturas-âncora desta aula: "Are we good to go?" (Estamos prontos para começar?), "Let me introduce you to our project lead." (Deixe-me apresentar o líder do projeto) e "Here are the next steps." (Estes são os próximos passos).

Frases curtas e diretas para fechar e iniciar sem deixar pontas soltas.

lessons.context: Great. I think we are good to go. We agree on the terms, so let's sign the contract. Now let me introduce you to our project lead. He will run the delivery team. The handoff will be seamless. Here are the next steps for the kickoff next week.

lessons.title: Pós-venda e expansão de conta
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz, em inglês simples, uma conversa de pós-venda com o cliente, revisa os resultados e abre espaço para novos projetos.
lessons.overview:
For Racional, delivering the project does not end the relationship; it is where the real partnership begins. The work of after-sales is about taking care of the client after delivery, doing a check-in and helping review the results of the project. This care is what sustains a long-term relationship with key accounts.

Think of a Google client whose data center Racional has just delivered. A simple conversation to hear whether everything went well against expectations and to measure client satisfaction shows that the company delivers on a promise. When the client is satisfied, they tend to renew and to trust the next step.

It is in after-sales that account expansion is born. By asking "What's next?" and presenting a roadmap, you open the way to new projects. The secret is to be proactive and stay close. This lesson gives you the language to turn a successful delivery into the start of the next contract.
lessons.intro:
Estruturas-âncora desta aula: "Let's review the results together." (Vamos revisar os resultados juntos), "We always deliver on our promise." (Sempre cumprimos o que prometemos) e "So, what's next for us?" (Então, o que vem a seguir?).

Presente simples, tom próximo e proativo: revise, confirme valor e abra a próxima porta.
lessons.situation: A Racional acabou de entregar um data center para um cliente da Google. Você faz um contato de pós-venda para revisar os resultados e falar do futuro.
lessons.context: Thank you for your trust. Let's review the results of the project. Everything went well against our plan. We are happy with your satisfaction. We always deliver on our promise. We want to stay close and be proactive. So, what's next for us? Let's talk about the roadmap.

vocab.example: Our after-sales care is strong.

lessons.title: Discovery calls & qualification
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz, em inglês, uma discovery call com um cliente norte-americano — fazendo perguntas abertas para entender a necessidade, o orçamento e quem decide. As instruções vêm em português; a prática, em inglês.
lessons.overview:
The discovery call is the first real conversation with a potential client. It is not the time to present Racional, but to listen: to understand what the client wants to build, the pain behind the project, and what they call success. For a North American director, a good discovery call shows that Racional thinks first about their problem and only then about the solution. That matters a lot in a direct business culture like the one in the United States.

In Racional's day-to-day, this conversation decides whether it is worth moving forward. A client like Microsoft or Amazon may approach the company for a hyperscale data center, but the team needs to know the budget, the timeline, and who the decision-maker is. Without that, the proposal goes out blind. As a member of the Executive Board, you do not always lead the sale, but you take part in these strategic conversations to qualify the opportunity and read whether the client is a good fit for the company.

The key is to ask open questions: "What's driving this project?" opens the client up; "Do you have a budget?" only gets a yes or no. Whoever asks well listens more and speaks less, and closes better deals. This lesson gives you the right questions to lead this moment in English, with the ease and presence of a senior executive.
lessons.intro:
Lembre três frases-âncora que vamos praticar: "What's driving this project?" (o que está motivando este projeto?), "What does success look like for you?" (como é o sucesso para você?) e "Who else is part of the decision?" (quem mais participa da decisão?).

São perguntas abertas e curtas. Você faz a pergunta, fica em silêncio e deixa o cliente falar.
lessons.situation: Um diretor de uma empresa de tecnologia dos EUA liga para a Racional sobre um possível data center no Brasil. É a primeira conversa, e você conduz a discovery call para entender o que ele precisa.
lessons.context: Thank you for the call today. Before we talk about Racional, I want to understand your project. What's driving this build right now? What does success look like for you? And who else is part of the decision? Your answers will help us see if we are a good fit.

vocab.example: The first discovery call is just to listen.

lessons.title: Sales enablement & coaching
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, em inglês, sobre como apoiar e treinar a equipe comercial — alinhar a mensagem, preparar o pitch e ajudar o time a lidar com objeções de clientes. As instruções vêm em português; a prática, em inglês.
lessons.overview:
Sales enablement is everything the company does to get the sales team ready to sell: training, materials, a clear message, and tools. Having good salespeople is not enough; they need to know how to tell Racional's story the same way, with the same arguments. For a senior executive, this is strategy: a well-prepared team closes more deals and protects the company's margin.

At Racional, this matters because every project is large and long, from 18 to 24 months. A rep who understands the company's track record and knows how to answer an objection from an American client conveys far more confidence. As a member of the Board, you help align on the message and coach the team, especially when the client is demanding and direct, like the company's North American clients.

This lesson gives you the vocabulary to talk about this behind-the-scenes work: to equip the team, to sharpen the message, to role-play a sales conversation, and to protect the margin. These are words you use when talking with the sales area or explaining to an international partner how Racional prepares its team.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar três ideias: "We equip the team with the right message." (equipamos o time com a mensagem certa), "We coach our reps to handle objections." (treinamos nossos vendedores para lidar com objeções) e "We protect the margin." (protegemos a margem).

Frases curtas e diretas. É assim que um sênior descreve o preparo do time.
lessons.situation: Um parceiro americano pergunta como a Racional prepara o time comercial para conversas difíceis com clientes. Você explica o trabalho de sales enablement e coaching.
lessons.context: We invest a lot in our sales team. First, we equip the team with the right message about our track record. Then we coach our reps and role-play hard conversations. So when a client raises an objection, they stay calm, and we protect the margin.

vocab.example: Sales enablement keeps the team ready.

lessons.title: Geopolitics: war, trade & global affairs
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conversa, em inglês, sobre geopolítica, comércio e tarifas com um cliente americano — de forma leve, neutra e conectando o tema ao mundo dos negócios. As instruções vêm em português; a prática, em inglês.
lessons.overview:
Geopolitics — wars, tariffs, trade, and sanctions — is a subject that comes up naturally in conversations with American executives. They follow global news and like to comment on how the world affects business. Knowing how to talk about this, without getting into controversy, creates connection and shows that you are an informed and well-read counterpart.

The secret is to keep neutral ground. You do not need to give a strong political opinion; it is enough to comment on the impact on the business world. For Racional, this is real: tariffs and problems in the supply chain affect the price of steel, equipment, and the components that go into a project or a data center. When an American client talks about global uncertainty, you can answer "from a business standpoint" and steer the conversation onto safe ground.

This is a relationship lesson (BRIDGE): the goal is to connect, not to give a lecture on politics. You will learn neutral and elegant phrases like "It's hard to predict." and "We stay flexible." — perfect for commenting on a sensitive topic and quickly returning to the business world.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar três frases neutras e seguras: "It's hard to predict." (é difícil prever), "From a business standpoint, we stay flexible." (do ponto de vista dos negócios, ficamos flexíveis) e "Tariffs affect our supply chain." (as tarifas afetam nossa cadeia de suprimentos).

Comente o tema, conecte aos negócios e volte ao terreno neutro. Nada de opinião política forte.
lessons.situation: Num jantar de relacionamento, um cliente americano comenta as últimas notícias sobre tarifas e guerra comercial. Você participa da conversa de forma leve e neutra.
lessons.context: Yes, the news on tariffs and trade is everywhere now. It's hard to predict what comes next. From a business standpoint, all this uncertainty touches our supply chain. So we try to stay flexible and diversify our suppliers. We don't take sides; we just plan ahead.

lessons.title: Construction industry overview
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta, em inglês, a Racional como uma construtora completa — seus segmentos, seu portfólio e seu modelo de entrega ponta a ponta. As instruções vêm em português; a prática, em inglês.
lessons.overview:
The construction industry has many companies, but few do everything from end to end. Racional is a general contractor: it handles the project from start to finish, with in-house engineering. Knowing how to present this in English, in a simple way, is what helps an American client quickly understand the size and strength of the company.

Racional has more than 50 years, 620+ projects, and over 10 million m² of built area. That is the track record that impresses. The company works in several segments: offices, healthcare facilities (such as hospitals), retail / shopping centers, hyperscale data centers, and industrial plants. Clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google come in precisely through the data center side.

The differentiator is the delivery model: Racional follows the project end to end, from feasibility to construction, with in-house engineering. This lesson gives you the vocabulary to present this overview in English — the kind of talk you use in a first meeting with an international client or on a site visit when explaining who Racional is.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar três frases-âncora: "We are a general contractor." (somos uma construtora geral), "We deliver projects end to end." (entregamos projetos de ponta a ponta) e "We have a strong track record." (temos um histórico forte).

Frases curtas que dão a dimensão da empresa em segundos.
lessons.situation: Numa primeira reunião, um cliente americano pede que você apresente a Racional. Você dá uma visão geral da empresa e dos seus segmentos de atuação.
lessons.context: Racional is a general contractor with more than fifty years in the construction industry. We work in many segments: offices, healthcare facilities, shopping centers, industrial plants, and hyperscale data centers. We have a strong track record and we deliver projects end to end with our in-house engineering.

lessons.title: Project lifecycle (design–build–handover)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreve, em inglês, as fases de um projeto de construção — do design ao build e ao handover — usando os marcos principais de cada etapa. As instruções vêm em português; a prática, em inglês.
lessons.overview:
The project lifecycle is the story of every building project, from beginning to end. It has three major phases: the design phase, the build phase, and the handover. Knowing how to name each phase in English is essential to talk with an American client who wants to know where their project stands.

Each phase has its milestones. The project begins with the groundbreaking (when you "break ground"). During the build, the team reports whether the project is on track. At the end come the final inspection, the punch list (items to fix), the commissioning of the systems, and finally the handover (handing over the keys). For Racional, in a Microsoft data center or a shopping center, this cycle lasts 18 to 24 months, and the client follows each milestone closely.

This lesson gives you the vocabulary to talk about each phase clearly. On a site visit or in a status meeting, the American client asks "are we on track?" and wants to hear the current milestone and the next step. You will learn to answer with simple technical terms, without losing fluency.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar três frases-âncora: "We break ground next month." (começamos as obras no próximo mês), "The project is on track." (o projeto está no prazo) e "We hand over the building in June." (entregamos o prédio em junho).

Use os marcos para situar o cliente em segundos: onde estamos e o que vem a seguir.
lessons.situation: Durante uma reunião de status, um cliente americano pergunta em que fase está o data center. Você explica as fases do projeto e o marco atual.
lessons.context: Let me walk you through the project lifecycle. The design phase is done. We broke ground in March, so we are now in the build phase. The project is on track. Next, we have the final inspection, the punch list, and commissioning. Then we hand over the building to you.

vocab.example: Every project has a clear lifecycle.

lessons.title: Site selection & feasibility studies
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, em inglês, sobre a escolha do terreno e o estudo de viabilidade — analisando localização, acesso, energia e retorno do investimento. As instruções vêm em português; a prática, em inglês.
lessons.overview:
Before any project comes a critical decision: where to build. Site selection and the feasibility study answer one simple question — is this project feasible or not? For an American client, seeing that Racional analyzes this with a method gives a lot of confidence right at the start of the relationship.

The study looks at several points: the location, the zoning (what the law allows you to build there), the access (roads), the power supply, and the flood risk. Each one can be a constraint. For a hyperscale data center from Microsoft or Amazon, the power supply is decisive: without strong and stable power, the site simply does not work. This careful work is what Racional does in the viability phase of its model.

In the end, it all comes down to the return on investment (ROI) and the land cost. This lesson gives you the vocabulary to lead this conversation with a client, explain the due diligence and the permitting, and show that Racional chooses the right site before investing.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar três frases-âncora: "We run a feasibility study first." (fazemos um estudo de viabilidade primeiro), "We assess the power supply and the flood risk." (avaliamos a energia e o risco de enchente) e "This site is feasible." (este terreno é viável).

Cada ponto avaliado vira um argumento de confiança para o cliente.
lessons.situation: Um cliente americano avalia construir um data center no Brasil e pergunta como a Racional escolhe o terreno. Você explica a site selection e o estudo de viabilidade.
lessons.context: Before we build, we run a feasibility study. We look at the location, the zoning, and the access. For a data center, the power supply is the key point. We also check the flood risk and the land cost. This way, we know if the site is feasible and good for your return on investment.

lessons.title: Foundations, soil & geotechnical
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explica fundações, solo e geotecnia em inglês simples, ligando cada decisão técnica a custo e prazo, durante uma visita técnica com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
The foundation is the first big decision of any project: it is where technical risk turns into cost risk. In hyperscale data centers and hospitals, strong segments for Racional, the weight of the equipment is enormous, and the soil must support that load safely. That is why everything starts with a soil survey, which measures the bearing capacity of the soil before designing the structure.

When the soil is weak near the surface, the engineering team chooses a deep foundation with piles that carry the load down to firm soil. In good soil, a shallow footing is enough. The right choice avoids settlement (sinking), a defect that is expensive to fix after the project is built.

For the North American client, who values directness, your role is not to give an engineering lecture, but to translate each term into business impact: why the foundation costs more, how much risk it removes, and how it protects the 18-to-24-month timeline of the project. Mastering this vocabulary lets you lead a site visit with ease and authority.
lessons.intro:
Antes de praticar, fixe três frases-âncora: "The soil survey showed weak soil here." / "To carry the load, we use deep piles." / "This prevents settlement later."

Use a estrutura simples: problema (solo) → solução (estacas) → benefício (sem recalque). Sempre conecte ao custo ou ao prazo.
lessons.situation: Durante uma visita ao canteiro de um data center, o cliente americano pergunta por que a fundação ficou mais cara do que ele esperava. Você explica a sondagem e a solução.
lessons.context: The soil survey showed weak soil near the surface. The bearing capacity is low here. To carry the load, we use deep piles. The piles reach firm ground. This costs more now, but it stops settlement later.

vocab.example: The foundation carries the whole building.

The bearing capacity is low here.
We use deep piles for support.

lessons.title: Family trips & vacation stories
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conversa sobre viagens em família e férias em inglês simples, criando conexão genuína com o cliente norte-americano nos momentos informais.
lessons.overview:
The relationship with a North American client does not happen only in the meeting room. During the 18 to 24 months of a Racional project, there are dinners, coffees, and hallway conversations where the long-term bond is really built. Talking about family trips and vacation is one of the most natural bridges for these moments.

Americans like light and sincere small talk before getting into serious matters. Asking "Any trips coming up?" or commenting on a road trip shows interest in the person, not just in the contract. Terms like to get away, to recharge, and the highlight keep the conversation smooth and warm.

For you, an executive with a packed schedule, this skill is worth gold: a few minutes of a well-handled personal conversation strengthen the trust that supports the entire business relationship. The goal here is not perfect grammar, but connection: listening, commenting, and sharing a short travel story naturally.
lessons.intro:
Guarde estas três frases-ponte: "Any trips coming up?" / "We took the kids to the beach. It was a much-needed break." / "The highlight was the food."

A ideia é responder com uma história curta e devolver a pergunta ao cliente. Mantenha leve e pessoal.
lessons.situation: Antes de uma reunião, o cliente americano comenta que acabou de voltar de férias com a família. Você puxa conversa sobre viagens para criar conexão.
lessons.context: Last month we took a road trip with the kids. We wanted to get away and recharge. The beach was the highlight. It was a much-needed break. Now I feel ready for work again. Any trips coming up for you?

lessons.title: Structural systems (concrete, steel, prefab)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explica os sistemas estruturais (concreto, aço e pré-fabricado) em inglês simples, ajudando o cliente norte-americano a entender a escolha por trás de custo e prazo.
lessons.overview:
After the foundation comes the structure: the skeleton that holds up the building. Racional works with different structural systems, and the choice between them changes the cost, the speed, and the flexibility of the project. It is a strategic decision that every executive in the sector needs to be able to explain.

The three most common paths are cast-in-place concrete, structural steel (with its steel frame), and precast or prefab (prefabricated parts). In shopping centers and industries, prefab usually speeds up the timeline; in data centers, steel allows large clear spans. The basic elements are always the same: columns, beams, and slabs.

For a North American client, who thinks about ROI and schedule, your value lies in linking the structural choice to the result: "steel costs more, but it delivers sooner," or "prefab reduces time on site." This vocabulary lets you lead a site visit and defend the engineering decisions with clarity.
lessons.intro:
Fixe estas frases-âncora: "We pour cast-in-place concrete here." / "The steel frame gives a big span." / "Precast parts are faster to build."

Pense sempre na troca: concreto (mais barato, mais lento) versus aço/pré-fabricado (mais rápido, vãos maiores). Conecte ao prazo.
lessons.situation: Numa visita técnica a uma obra de shopping center, o cliente americano pergunta por que a Racional escolheu pré-fabricado em vez de concreto moldado no local. Você explica a vantagem de prazo.
lessons.context: This building uses a steel frame. The steel gives us a big span with fewer columns. For the parking area, we use precast parts. Precast is faster to build on site. Cast-in-place concrete costs less, but it takes more time.

lessons.title: MEP systems (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala sobre os sistemas prediais (mecânica, elétrica e hidráulica) em inglês simples, explicando ao cliente norte-americano por que eles são vitais em data centers e hospitais.
lessons.overview:
After the structure, what makes the building work are the MEP systems (mechanical, electrical, and plumbing). In hyperscale data centers for clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google, and in hospitals, these systems are not a detail: they are the heart of the project. This is where Racional adds the most technical value.

The HVAC and cooling keep the servers cool; the electrical systems and the backup generators ensure power at all times. The key concepts are redundancy (having a backup) and uptime (staying running without stopping). Everything runs through ductwork and wiring, and requires to coordinate systems so that nothing conflicts.

For the North American client, these systems are critical: a power outage in a data center costs millions. Your role is to show, in simple English, that Racional understands this criticality and delivers redundancy and high uptime. This vocabulary lets you lead technical conversations with confidence.
lessons.intro:
Fixe estas frases-âncora: "The cooling keeps the servers cold." / "We have backup generators for redundancy." / "This protects the uptime."

A lógica é simples: sistema → reserva (redundancy) → resultado (uptime). Conecte sempre ao risco do cliente.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião com um cliente americano de data center, ele pergunta como a Racional garante que a energia e a refrigeração nunca falhem. Você explica os sistemas e a redundância.
lessons.context: A data center needs strong MEP systems. The cooling keeps the servers cold. We have backup generators for the power. This is redundancy: we always have a spare. It protects the uptime, so the data center never stops.

lessons.title: Building codes & permitting
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala sobre normas e licenciamento (building codes e permits) em inglês simples, explicando ao cliente norte-americano como a Racional protege o prazo cumprindo as regras.
lessons.overview:
No project moves forward without complying with public rules. The building codes and the permits define what can be built, where, and how. The permitting process is a stage that can delay the whole schedule if it is not well managed, something Racional handles with great care.

The American client knows this world well: in the U.S., code-compliant, zoning, and inspection are part of the daily vocabulary. Terms like approval, occupancy permit, and compliance show that the project follows the rules from start to finish, all the way to delivery.

Your role as an executive is to convey confidence: Racional handles permitting early so it does not stall the schedule and ensures everything stays code-compliant. In projects of 18 to 24 months, delaying a permit is costly. This vocabulary lets you talk about regulation naturally and protect the relationship with the key account.

Fixe estas frases-âncora: "We need a permit before we start." / "The design is code-compliant." / "We handle the permitting early to protect the schedule."

A lógica é: regra (code) → licença (permit) → aprovação (approval). Conecte sempre ao prazo.

lessons.title: Vertical transportation (elevators, traffic study)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala sobre transporte vertical (elevadores e estudo de tráfego) em inglês simples, ligando o desempenho dos elevadores à experiência do usuário do cliente norte-americano.

In tall office buildings, shopping centers, and hospitals, vertical transportation defines the experience of the people who use the building. Elevators and escalators need to move a lot of people without lines, and this is designed, not improvised.

It all starts with a traffic study, which measures the flow at the peak hour to define the capacity and the number of elevators. The goal is to reduce the wait time and avoid the bottleneck in the lobby. It is a topic that directly connects engineering and user experience.

For the North American client, who thinks about occupancy and satisfaction, showing that Racional sizes vertical transportation based on data is a differentiator. This vocabulary lets you explain, in simple English, why the building will have a comfortable flow even during the busiest hours.

lessons.title: American humor, idioms & slang
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai entender e usar expressões informais e de humor leve comuns no dia a dia de negócios nos Estados Unidos.
lessons.overview:
Humor and informal expressions are the glue of business conversations in the United States. North American clients use short phrases like to touch base (to check in quickly) or a heads-up (an early warning) all the time. These are not hard slang: they are friendly shortcuts that keep the conversation light. For a Racional director who talks with clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google, understanding these expressions avoids misunderstandings and shows that you keep up with the rhythm of the conversation.

Many of these phrases come up even before the meeting starts. A client may say let's touch base next week or I'm slammed today (I'm swamped with work today). Instead of translating word for word, the secret is to recognize the intention: to set up a contact, to ask for patience, or simply to break the ice (to break the ice). When you return one of these expressions naturally, the client feels they are talking with someone who is in the game.

In this unit you will practice a small set of useful expressions for the long-term relationship with Racional's key accounts. The goal is not to memorize rare slang, but to recognize and confidently use a handful of phrases that show up every week in emails, calls, and coffees with the American client. That way, even in simple English, you sound close and comfortable.
lessons.intro:
Vamos relembrar três frases-âncora que você vai usar na prática: Let's touch base next week. (Vamos nos falar semana que vem.), Thanks for the heads-up. (Obrigado pelo aviso.) e No worries. (Sem problema.).

Essas expressões são curtas e diretas. Use-as para soar natural e próximo do cliente.
lessons.situation: Antes de uma call com um cliente norte-americano, ele manda uma mensagem curta com algumas expressões informais. Você precisa entender e responder no mesmo tom leve.

I am on the fence about one thing, but it is a small point. Let's talk soon. No worries about the time. We can be flexible.

lessons.title: Office towers & commercial buildings
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai usar o vocabulário básico de torres de escritórios e prédios comerciais para falar com clientes norte-americanos.
lessons.overview:
Office towers are one of Racional's main segments. An office tower or commercial building is much more than a tall building: it is a product that companies lease to work in. That is why words like tenant and leasable area come up all the time in conversations with clients and investors.

When Racional delivers an office tower, the client thinks about value. A column-free floor gives more usable space, and good amenities (such as a gym and a restaurant) attract more companies. The LEED certification (green certification) shows that the building is sustainable, something highly valued by North American clients like Microsoft and Google. Knowing how to explain these points in simple English helps you show Racional's differentiator.

In this unit you will learn how to present an office tower on a site visit with an international client. You do not need difficult terms: with a short, clear vocabulary, you describe the floor, the leasable space, and the amenities, and answer basic questions about occupancy. This is the kind of conversation that opens doors to new long-term contracts.
lessons.intro:
Relembre estas frases-âncora: This is our office tower. (Esta é a nossa torre de escritórios.), The floor is column-free. (O andar é sem colunas.) e The building has good amenities. (O prédio tem boas comodidades.).

Use frases curtas e mostre o valor para o cliente.
lessons.situation: Você conduz um cliente norte-americano numa visita a uma torre de escritórios entregue pela Racional e explica os pontos fortes do prédio.
lessons.context: Welcome to our office tower. This is a modern commercial building. The floor is column-free, so the space is open. The building has good amenities. It has a gym and a restaurant. We also have LEED certification. The leasable area is large. Many tenants want to work here.

lessons.title: Hospital construction & healthcare facilities
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai usar o vocabulário básico de construção hospitalar para falar com clientes norte-americanos sobre segurança e qualidade.
lessons.overview:
Hospital construction is one of Racional's most technical and sensitive segments. In a healthcare facility, everything revolves around patient safety. Spaces like the operating room and the ICU require special care with cleanliness, air, and power. That is why this type of project has rules that cannot be broken.

A delicate point is that many hospitals keep operating during the construction. Racional needs to phase construction (do the work in stages) to ensure operational continuity and reduce downtime. Infection control, or infection control, is an absolute priority: it is a non-negotiable item. Knowing how to explain this care in English shows the client that Racional understands the complexity of the healthcare sector.

In this unit you will practice how to describe Racional's hospital expertise to a North American client. With simple sentences, you will talk about patient safety, infection control, and phased construction. This vocabulary is essential to convey confidence in a segment where any mistake has serious consequences.
lessons.intro:
Relembre estas frases-âncora: Patient safety is our priority. (A segurança do paciente é nossa prioridade.), We phase the construction. (Nós fazemos a obra por etapas.) e Infection control is non-negotiable. (O controle de infecção é inegociável.).

Use frases curtas e firmes para mostrar cuidado e confiança.
lessons.situation: Você conversa com um cliente norte-americano da área de saúde e explica como a Racional constrói hospitais com segurança, mesmo com a unidade em funcionamento.
lessons.context: We build hospitals and healthcare facilities. Patient safety is our priority. Infection control is non-negotiable. The operating room and the ICU need clean air. Sometimes the hospital is open during the work. So we phase the construction. This way, there is little downtime. The hospital can keep working.

lessons.title: Shopping centers & retail
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai usar o vocabulário básico de shopping centers e varejo para falar com clientes e investidores norte-americanos.
lessons.overview:
Shopping centers are an important segment for Racional, and they have a logic of their own. A shopping center lives on foot traffic: the more people circulate, the more value for the stores. That is why the tenant mix and the presence of an anchor store (a major brand that draws crowds) are strategic decisions that the client follows closely.

When Racional builds a shopping center, it delivers much more than walls. It delivers common areas, a food court, retail space, and parking capacity. All of this affects the occupancy rate and the success of the grand opening. Talking about these points in simple English helps you show that Racional thinks about the client's business, not just the construction.

In this unit you will practice how to present a shopping center project to a North American client. With a few key words, you will describe the tenant mix, the foot traffic, and the final delivery. This is the vocabulary that connects Racional's engineering to the client's return on investment.
lessons.intro:
Relembre estas frases-âncora: The anchor store brings foot traffic. (A loja-âncora traz fluxo de pessoas.), We have a good tenant mix. (Temos um bom mix de lojas.) e The handover is on time. (A entrega está no prazo.).

Use frases curtas e conecte a obra ao negócio do cliente.

lessons.title: Data centers (cooling, redundancy, Tier)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai usar o vocabulário básico de data centers para falar com clientes norte-americanos de tecnologia.
lessons.overview:
Data centers are one of Racional's fastest-growing segments, and the clients are technology giants like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. In a data center, what matters most is uptime (the system running) and reducing downtime (time stopped). These buildings cannot stop, and that is why the client talks about a highly demanding, critical project.

To keep everything running, the data center needs redundancy (backup systems), a good cooling system, and a backup generator. The Tier classification measures the building's level of reliability: the higher the Tier, the safer it is. Racional needs to deliver a scalable design (a design that can grow) to keep up with the demand of hyperscale clients.

In this unit you will practice how to talk about data centers with a North American technology client. With simple vocabulary, you will explain cooling, redundancy, and Tier. This is the segment where technical precision and confidence in English make a big difference in closing long-term contracts.
lessons.intro:
Relembre estas frases-âncora: Uptime is very important. (O tempo no ar é muito importante.), We have full redundancy. (Temos redundância total.) e The cooling system is strong. (O sistema de resfriamento é forte.).

Use frases curtas e técnicas, sem complicar.
lessons.situation: Você conversa com um cliente norte-americano de tecnologia sobre um projeto de data center e explica os pontos críticos do prédio.
lessons.context: This is our data center. Uptime is very important. The client cannot have downtime. So we have full redundancy. We have a strong cooling system. There is a backup generator for power. This is a Tier 3 data center. The design is scalable, so the client can grow.

lessons.title: Sports as common ground
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai usar vocabulário simples de esportes para criar conexão em conversas informais com clientes norte-americanos.
lessons.overview:
In the United States, talking about sports is one of the easiest ways to create connection. Before or after a meeting, a client may ask did you catch the game? or say which team they support, to root for. This light chat, the small talk, opens space for a closer relationship, which is what sustains Racional's 18-to-24-month contracts.

You do not need to be an expert in American sports. A simple vocabulary is enough: fan, season, the score, and playoffs (the final stage). Knowing how to say that a game was a close one or commenting what a finish already shows genuine interest. And you can bring Brazilian soccer into the conversation, creating a natural cultural exchange.

In this unit you will practice how to join a conversation about sports with a North American client. The goal is not heavy grammar, but sounding natural and friendly. This kind of personal connection turns a purely professional relationship into a long-term partnership.
lessons.intro:
Relembre estas frases-âncora: Did you catch the game? (Você viu o jogo?), Which team do you root for? (Para que time você torce?) e What a finish! (Que final incrível!).

Use frases curtas e mostre interesse genuíno no cliente.
lessons.situation: Antes de uma reunião, o cliente norte-americano começa a falar do jogo de ontem. Você entra no papo de forma leve e amigável.
lessons.context: Hi Cassio. Did you catch the game last night? It was a close one. My team won, but it was hard. I always root for them. The season is exciting now. We are in the playoffs. What a finish! Do you follow any sport in Brazil? I know soccer is very big there.

I root for this team.

lessons.title: Industrial facilities & manufacturing plants
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá descrever uma planta industrial e seus principais elementos em inglês durante uma visita técnica com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
Industrial facilities (industrial facilities) and manufacturing plants (manufacturing plants) are one of the five core segments at Racional, alongside offices, hospitals, shopping centers, and data centers. When a client like Amazon or a major manufacturer hires the construction company, they don't just want walls: they want a space that supports an efficient production line (production line), with well-designed material flow (material flow) and load capacity (load capacity) suited to the machinery.

In day-to-day executive work, talking about this topic in English means guiding the client through the site and explaining design decisions: the clear height (clear height) that allows more product to be stacked, the floor plan (floor plan) that reduces bottlenecks (bottleneck), and the utilities (utilities) - power, water, compressed air - that keep the operation running. For a Racional director, this vocabulary is the bridge between engineering and the business conversation.

The North American client values clarity and data. When you say, naturally, that a warehouse (warehouse) has high throughput (throughput) or that it's possible to retrofit the plant (to retrofit) for a new shift (shift), you show technical command and confidence. That's what sets Racional apart as a long-term partner in 18- to 24-month projects.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar frases simples para uma visita à obra. Lembre destas estruturas: This is our production line. / The clear height is 12 meters. / We can retrofit the plant for a new shift.

Use o presente simples e frases curtas. O objetivo é apontar e explicar, não fazer discursos longos.
lessons.situation: Você acompanha um cliente norte-americano em uma visita à fábrica em construção e explica a planta e a linha de produção.
lessons.context: This is our new manufacturing plant. The floor plan is simple and clear. The production line is on the right. We have a big warehouse for storage. The clear height is twelve meters. This helps the material flow. We can scale production for a second shift. The plant is fast and safe.

lessons.title: Procurement & imports (containers, lead time)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá falar sobre compras, importação e prazos de entrega em inglês com fornecedores e clientes norte-americanos.
lessons.overview:
On large projects like data centers or shopping centers, procurement (procurement) defines whether deadlines are met. Racional buys from suppliers (suppliers) in Brazil and abroad, and much of the equipment arrives through imports. Each item has a lead time (lead time) that has to enter the schedule long before the site needs it.

When a piece of equipment comes from abroad, it travels in a container (container), goes through customs clearance (customs clearance), and stays in transit (in transit) for weeks. A delay (delay) at customs can stop an entire work front. That's why the team uses a buffer (buffer) in the planning and sometimes keeps a backup supplier (backup supplier) to reduce supply chain (supply chain) risk.

For the North American client, who values punctuality, speaking well about this topic conveys control. Knowing how to say in English when a purchase order (purchase order) was placed, what the freight (freight) is, and when the shipment (shipment) arrives helps the Racional executive give the project predictability and protect the long-term relationship.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar frases de status de compras e importação. Âncoras: We placed the order last week. / The lead time is eight weeks. / The container is in transit now.

Use presente e passado simples. Frases curtas e diretas funcionam melhor com o cliente.
lessons.situation: Você atualiza um cliente norte-americano sobre o status de um equipamento importado que está a caminho da obra.
lessons.context: We placed the purchase order last month. The lead time is eight weeks. The container is in transit now. It will arrive at the port soon. Then we start customs clearance. We have a buffer for any delay. We also have a backup supplier. The supply chain is under control.

lessons.title: Quality control & specifications
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá falar sobre controle de qualidade, especificações e inspeções em inglês durante a obra com clientes norte-americanos.
lessons.overview:
Quality is Racional's hallmark across more than 620 projects and 50 years of history. Quality control (quality control) means making sure everything follows the specifications (specifications) and standards (standards) agreed with the client. In hospitals and data centers, where mistakes are costly, this care is even more critical.

Day to day, the team runs inspections (inspection) using a checklist (checklist). If something is not right - a defect (defect) or a non-conformity (non-conformity) - the work has to be redone (rework) and re-inspected (to re-inspect). Everything stays within the tolerance (tolerance) accepted by the project. At the end of each stage, there is a formal sign-off (sign-off).

The North American client expects clear processes and traceability (traceability). When the Racional executive explains in English that the work meets the standard (to meet the standard) and shows the punch list (punch list) before handover, they build trust and reinforce the company's reputation as a long-term partner.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar frases de qualidade e inspeção. Âncoras: The work meets the standard. / We found one defect. / We need the sign-off today.

Use presente simples e termos curtos. Foque em ser claro sobre o que está certo e o que precisa de rework.
lessons.situation: Você conduz uma inspeção de qualidade com um cliente norte-americano e revisa a lista de pendências antes da entrega.
lessons.context: Quality control is very important for us. We follow the specifications and the standards. Today we do an inspection with a checklist. We found one small defect. We will fix it with rework. Then we re-inspect the area. The work meets the standard now. We are ready for the sign-off.

We follow the client specifications.

lessons.title: Schedule management & critical path
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá falar sobre cronograma, prazos e caminho crítico em inglês com clientes norte-americanos.
lessons.overview:
The schedule (schedule) is the heart of any Racional project. On 18- to 24-month projects, every milestone (milestone) and every deadline (deadline) must be respected in order to deliver on time (to deliver on time). The critical path (critical path) shows the tasks that cannot slip without moving the final date.

Day to day, the executive needs to know how to say whether the project is on track (on track), ahead of schedule (ahead of schedule), or behind schedule (behind schedule). When a task slips (to slip), the team uses the float (float) or rushes to catch up (to catch up). Understanding the dependencies (dependency) between phases (phase) is what keeps the data center or shopping center on the agreed timeline (timeline).

The North American client places enormous value on punctuality. When the Racional executive flags a risk (to flag a risk) early, in simple words, they protect trust and show management maturity. Talking about the schedule in English is talking about credibility.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar frases de status de cronograma. Âncoras: The project is on track. / We are two days behind schedule. / We will catch up next week.

Use presente e futuro simples. O cliente quer saber: estamos no prazo ou não?
lessons.situation: Você dá ao cliente norte-americano uma atualização semanal sobre o andamento do cronograma da obra.
lessons.context: The project is on track. We reached the first milestone last week. The next deadline is in ten days. One task is a little behind schedule. But we have some float on this phase. We will catch up soon. The critical path is safe. We will deliver on time.

lessons.title: American sports (NFL, NBA, MLB, golf)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá conversar de forma leve sobre esportes americanos com clientes dos EUA para criar conexão.
lessons.overview:
Sports is one of the easiest and most powerful topics for building a connection (connection) with a North American client. In the U.S., football (NFL), basketball (NBA), baseball (MLB), and golf are part of everyday life and business conversations. Knowing how to start this kind of small talk makes the relationship more human, away from the technical agenda of the project.

For the Racional executive, who maintains long-term relationships with key accounts over 18 to 24 months, commenting on a game (to catch the game) or asking about the client's team (team) opens doors. Many Americans are die-hard fans (die-hard fan) and love to talk about the playoffs (playoffs) or a close game (a close game). It's small talk that builds trust.

You don't need to be an expert. You just need to know how to say which team you root for (to root for), ask about the season (season), and show genuine interest. In golf, a lot of business happens on the course - inviting the client to play a round (to hit the course) can be worth more than a formal meeting.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar small talk de esportes. Âncoras: Did you catch the game last night? / Which team do you root for? / It was a close game.

O tom é leve e amigável. O objetivo é conectar, não acertar gramática difícil.

lessons.title: Cost control & budget tracking
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá falar sobre orçamento, controle de custos e acompanhamento financeiro em inglês com clientes norte-americanos.
lessons.overview:
Cost control (cost control) is what protects the margin and the trust in every Racional project. The budget (budget) defines how much the project can spend, and the team's job is to keep everything on budget (on budget). On large projects, like hyperscale data centers, a small cost overrun (cost overrun) can add up to millions.

Day to day, the team compares the planned cost with the actual cost (actual cost) and watches the variance (variance). When there is a deviation, it's time to close the gap (to close the gap), use the contingency (contingency), or revise the forecast (forecast). Tracking (to track) the main cost drivers (cost driver) keeps the project healthy and the cash flow (cash flow) under control.

The North American client values financial transparency and a focus on ROI. When the Racional executive says clearly in English that the project is on budget, or explains a variance early, they convey governance and accountability. Talking about cost with confidence is speaking the language of the client's board.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar frases de status financeiro. Âncoras: The project is on budget. / The variance is small. / We will close the gap this month.

Use presente e futuro simples. O cliente quer saber: estamos dentro do orçamento?
lessons.situation: Você apresenta ao cliente norte-americano o status de custos do projeto na reunião mensal.
lessons.context: The project is on budget. The actual cost is close to the forecast. The variance is very small. We track every cost driver each week. We have some contingency for risks. There is no cost overrun now. We will close the gap soon. The cash flow is healthy.

lessons.title: Health, Safety & Environment on-site
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá falar sobre segurança e saúde no canteiro de obras em inglês, usando termos técnicos simples ao receber clientes norte-americanos.
lessons.overview:
Site safety is one of the first things North American clients assess when choosing a construction company. In the United States, the culture of safety (seguranca) is taken very seriously, and companies like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google demand a zero-risk posture from their partners. For Racional, with more than 620 projects and 50 years of history, talking about safety naturally in English shows maturity and governance.

The core terms in this lesson describe daily life on the site: PPE / personal protective equipment (equipamento de protecao individual), the hazard (perigo) that must be controlled, the toolbox talk (a quick safety talk at the start of the shift), and the zero-harm policy (politica de dano zero). You will also talk about compliance (conformidade com as regras) and the incident rate (indice de acidentes), a number every American client asks for.

When you host a client at a hyperscale data center or hospital site, the safety briefing opens the visit. Saying in plain English "safety is our first priority" and explaining how Racional carries out its risk assessment (avaliacao de risco) conveys trust. This lesson prepares you for that moment: few words, short and direct sentences, exactly as the American executive expects.
lessons.intro:
Nesta prática vamos usar três frases-âncora simples: Safety is our first priority. / Everyone must wear PPE on-site. / We have a zero-harm policy.

Repare que todas estão no presente simples e são curtas. Esse é o tom que você usa com o cliente.
lessons.situation: Você recebe um cliente norte-americano de um projeto de data center e faz a abertura de segurança antes da visita ao canteiro.
lessons.context: Welcome to our site. Safety is our first priority here. Before we start, please put on your PPE. This means a hard hat, a safety vest, and safety glasses. We have a zero-harm policy. This means we want zero accidents. Every morning, the team has a short toolbox talk. We talk about the risks of the day. Our incident rate is very low, and we are proud of it. Please follow me and watch your step.

lessons.title: Commissioning & handover
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá explicar a fase de comissionamento e entrega da obra em inglês, usando termos simples com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
The end of a project is as important as the beginning. The commissioning (comissionamento) phase is when Racional tests all of the building's systems to make sure everything works. Then comes the handover (entrega), the moment when the client receives the finished building. For North American clients in data centers or hospitals, this phase must be clear and well documented.

At this stage, everyday terms come up: the punch list (lista de pendencias), each snag (small defect to fix), the as-built drawings (desenhos do como foi construido), and the warranty (garantia). When everything is in order, the client can sign off on (dar o aceite formal) and the building becomes ready for occupancy (pronto para ocupacao).

Talking about this in English shows the client that Racional closes the project with governance and accountability. In an 18- to 24-month cycle, the handover is the moment that shapes the client's final perception and the chance for new projects. This lesson gives you the simple phrases to lead that conversation with confidence.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar três frases-âncora: We are ready for handover. / The building is fully operational. / Please sign off on the punch list.

São frases curtas que você usa no fim do projeto, com clareza.
lessons.situation: Você conduz a reunião final de entrega de um data center com o cliente norte-americano e confirma que a obra está pronta.
lessons.context: Good morning. Today is our handover day. We tested all the systems last week. Everything works well now. The building is fully operational. We have a short punch list with a few small snags. Our team will fix them this week. Here are the as-built drawings and all the documentation. The warranty starts today. The building is ready for occupancy. Please sign off on the final report. Thank you for your trust.

lessons.title: Site visit em inglês
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá conduzir uma visita ao canteiro em inglês, guiando o cliente e mostrando o andamento da obra.
lessons.overview:
The site visit (visita ao canteiro) is one of the most important moments in the client relationship. It's when the North American client walks through the project, sees the progress, and feels confident in the partner. For Racional, which builds offices, hospitals, shopping centers, and data centers, guiding that visit naturally in English makes all the difference.

You will use short, practical guiding phrases: follow me (me siga), watch your step (cuidado com o degrau), this way (por aqui), and over here (aqui, deste lado). You will also point out parts of the project, such as the foundation (fundacao), the structure (estrutura), and each floor (andar/pavimento), as well as comment on the progress (andamento) and say that everything is on schedule (dentro do prazo).

This vocabulary turns a technical visit into a smooth conversation. When the client from Microsoft or Amazon walks through the data center and hears you explain each stage in simple English, they sense organization and command. This lesson prepares you to guide the visit from start to finish, with confidence and courtesy.
lessons.intro:
As frases-âncora desta aula são de guia: Please follow me. / Watch your step. / We are on schedule.

Use-as com gestos simples enquanto caminha com o cliente.
lessons.situation: Você guia um cliente norte-americano pela obra de um shopping center e mostra o andamento de cada andar.
lessons.context: Welcome to the site. Please put on your hard hat and your safety vest. Now, please follow me. Watch your step here. This way, please. Over here is the foundation. It is very strong. Now let's go up. This is the first floor. We are on schedule. The structure is ready. Let's take a look at the progress on this floor. Everything looks good. Let me walk you through the next area.

Please put on your hard hat.
You need a safety vest here.

The structure is ready.
We are on schedule.

lessons.title: Personal hobbies & sports (cycling, swimming, walking)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá conversar sobre hobbies e esportes em inglês simples, criando conexão com o cliente fora das reuniões.
lessons.overview:
Not every important conversation happens in the meeting room. With North American clients, small talk (conversa informal) about hobbies (hobbies) and sports creates real rapport. In a project cycle of 18 to 24 months, these light moments between site work and dinners help build a long-term relationship of trust.

This lesson brings simple vocabulary to talk about activities like cycling (ciclismo), swimming (natacao), and hiking. You will learn useful expressions such as to be into something (curtir/gostar muito de algo), to work out (treinar/se exercitar), to stay active (manter-se ativo), and to clear my head (espairecer). These are short phrases that sound natural over coffee or in the car on the way to the site.

Americans often appreciate people who take care of their health and keep an active routine. Knowing how to say what you like to do on weekends, or asking about the client's favorite sport, opens doors and humanizes the relationship. Here the focus is not heavy grammar, but genuine connection in simple English.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora desta conversa: I'm into cycling. / I work out to stay active. / What do you do to unwind?

Use-as com tom leve, como numa conversa de café.
lessons.situation: Depois de uma reunião, você toma um café com o cliente norte-americano e conversa sobre esportes e fim de semana.
lessons.context: On the weekend, I like to stay active. I'm into cycling. I ride my bike for one hour. I also like swimming. It helps me clear my head. Sometimes I just go for a walk outdoors. It is a nice way to unwind after a busy week. I try to work out three times a week. It keeps me fit. What about you? What do you do to relax on the weekend?

lessons.title: Sustainability & green building (LEED)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá falar sobre construção sustentável e certificação LEED em inglês simples, conectando o tema ao valor do projeto.
lessons.overview:
Sustainable construction is now a central criterion for North American clients. Companies like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google have carbon targets and want partners who deliver green buildings. For Racional, talking about sustainability (sustentabilidade) and green building (construcao verde) in English shows that the company is aligned with the global agenda.

This lesson brings the vocabulary of the topic: the LEED certification (certificacao LEED), energy-efficient (eficientes em energia) buildings, reducing the carbon footprint (pegada de carbono), the use of renewable energy (energia renovavel) and low-carbon materials (materiais de baixo carbono). You will also connect this to the business: green buildings lower operating costs (custos de operacao) and raise asset value (valor do ativo).

For a board-level executive, this is a strategic message. Showing the client that the investment in sustainability pays off (se paga, da retorno) over time connects the technical topic to ROI. This lesson gives you simple phrases to defend that value in a conversation with the American client.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora desta aula: Our building is energy-efficient. / We use renewable energy. / Green building pays off over time.

São frases curtas que ligam sustentabilidade a valor.
lessons.situation: Você apresenta a um cliente norte-americano por que o novo escritório será uma construção verde com certificação LEED.
lessons.context: Sustainability is very important to us. This new office is a green building. It will have LEED certification. The building is energy-efficient. We use renewable energy, like solar power. We also use low-carbon materials. This reduces the carbon footprint. A green building has lower operating costs. It also has a higher asset value. In the end, green building pays off over time. It is good for the planet and good for business.

lessons.title: BIM & construction tech
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá falar sobre BIM e tecnologia de construção em inglês simples, explicando seus benefícios ao cliente.
lessons.overview:
Technology has changed the way we build. The digital model (modelo digital), known as BIM, is now at the heart of large projects. For North American clients in data centers and hospitals, seeing that Racional uses a single source of truth (uma unica fonte de verdade) with all the project's data conveys trust and modernity.

In this lesson you will talk about tools that are easy to explain: clash detection (deteccao de conflitos entre projetos), the coordination of the MEP disciplines (mechanical, electrical, and plumbing), 4D scheduling (cronograma em 4D, linking the model to time), and the drone survey (levantamento por drone). You will also see prefabrication (pre-fabricacao) and modular construction (construcao modular), which speed up the work.

The core benefit is clear: technology helps you flag a conflict (apontar um conflito) before construction begins, avoiding the do-over (retrabalho). For an executive, that means less risk, lower cost, and deadlines met. This lesson gives you simple phrases to show the client how technology protects the project.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora desta aula: We use a digital model. / It is our single source of truth. / We find conflicts before we build.

Frases curtas que mostram o valor da tecnologia.
lessons.situation: Você apresenta a um cliente norte-americano como a Racional usa BIM e tecnologia para reduzir risco no projeto de um data center.
lessons.context: We use a lot of technology in our projects. First, we build a digital model. This model is our single source of truth. All the teams use the same data. We use clash detection to find conflicts early. For example, we check the MEP systems. If we find a conflict, we flag it before we build. This saves time and money. We also use drone survey to check the progress. And we use prefabrication to build faster. Technology helps us reduce risk.

lessons.title: Subcontractor management
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala sobre gestão de subcontratados em inglês simples — como a Racional escolhe, integra e acompanha seus parceiros de obra — numa conversa com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
No Racional project is built by Racional alone. On a hyperscale data center for Microsoft or a large hospital, dozens of specialized companies work together: electrical, HVAC, foundations, facade. Each one is a subcontractor (subcontratado), responsible for a trade (especialidade tecnica). Knowing how to talk about this chain in English is essential, because the American client wants to understand who does what and how quality is guaranteed.

The cycle begins long before the site. Racional needs to pre-qualify (pre-qualificar) and to vet (avaliar/checar) each company before hiring, then carry out the scope handoff (passagem de escopo) clearly. During the work, the site supervisor (supervisor de campo) keeps everyone to a standard (no padrao) and manages the interface (interface/conexao) between teams. At the end of each stage, a snag list (lista de pendencias) records what still needs to be fixed.

For a Racional Board executive, this vocabulary communicates governance and risk control. When you say, in clear English, that the company pre-qualifies suppliers and that a supervisor is accountable for the result - to own the outcome (assumir o resultado) - the American client senses process maturity. That's what sustains 18- to 24-month relationships with key accounts.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar três estruturas-âncora simples: "We pre-qualify every subcontractor.", "The site supervisor coordinates all trades." e "We hold them to one standard."

Repita essas frases em voz alta. Elas serão a base da sua conversa de hoje.
lessons.situation: Numa site visit, um cliente americano pergunta como a Racional controla a qualidade das empresas que trabalham na obra. Você explica o processo, do começo ao fim.
lessons.context: We do not build alone. On a big project, many companies work with us. Each company has one trade. Before we hire, we pre-qualify and vet them. Then we do a clear scope handoff. On site, the site supervisor coordinates all the trades. He holds every team to one standard. At the end of each stage, we make a snag list. We fix the small problems on the list. We own the outcome. The client trusts our process.
