lessons.title: Meeting fundamentals: agenda, minutes, action items
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz a estrutura de uma reunião em inglês simples — define a pauta, registra as decisões e distribui os action items — com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
Well-run meetings are the heart of Module 4. In monthly and biweekly meetings with clients like Amazon or Google, Racional needs to show that it controls both time and decisions. It all starts with the agenda (pauta): a clear list of agenda items (itens de pauta) that keeps everyone focused and respects an executive's packed schedule.

During the meeting, someone needs to take minutes (registrar a ata) - to note what was decided. Each decision becomes an action item (item de acao) with an owner (responsavel) and a due date (prazo). If a topic doesn't fit right now, you can to park (deixar de lado) it and send it to the parking lot (lista de pendencias para depois), without wasting the meeting's time.

The American client values punctuality and clarity. When you keep everyone to time (mantem todos no horario) and then send a recap email (e-mail de resumo) with who does what and by when - by end of day (ate o fim do dia), for example - you project the governance that the Racional Board represents. That's how meetings turn into real action.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora de hoje: "Let's start with the agenda.", "I'll take the minutes." e "Each action item has an owner and a due date."

Repita-as. Elas estruturam qualquer reunião em inglês.
lessons.situation: Você abre uma reunião quinzenal com o cliente americano. Precisa definir a pauta, controlar o tempo e fechar com os action items claros.
lessons.context: Let's start with the agenda. We have three agenda items today. I will take the minutes. For each decision, we set an action item. Every action item has an owner and a due date. Please keep us to time. If a topic is too big now, we park it. We put it in the parking lot for later. After the meeting, I send a recap email. The email lists who does what and by when. This way, the meeting turns into action.

The first agenda item is the budget.
I send the minutes after the meeting.
I will take the minutes today.
Each action item has an owner.
Who is the owner of this task?

We put it in the parking lot.

Please send it by end of day.

lessons.title: Holidays & traditions (Thanksgiving, July 4th)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conversa com naturalidade sobre feriados e tradições americanas — como Thanksgiving e o Quatro de Julho — criando conexão genuína com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
In 18- to 24-month projects, the relationship with the American client runs largely on light conversations. Knowing how to talk about holidays like Thanksgiving (Dia de Acao de Gracas) and the Fourth of July (Quatro de Julho) opens human doors that no technical report can. These are dates when families gather (se reunem) and show gratitude (gratidao).

These holidays have simple symbols that are easy to comment on: the turkey (peru) at Thanksgiving, the fireworks (fogos de artificio) and cookouts (churrascos ao ar livre) on the Fourth of July. Many Americans use the long weekend (feriado prolongado) for a road trip (viagem de carro) or to recharge (recarregar as energias) with family.

For the Racional executive, mentioning these topics at the start of a call or dinner creates connection. Asking "Did you host Thanksgiving this year?" shows genuine interest and cultural care. That's exactly what sets apart purely functional communication from a relationship of trust with North American key accounts.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora leves: "How was your Thanksgiving?", "Did you do anything for the Fourth of July?" e "It's a long weekend, time to recharge."

O tom aqui é leve e amigável, não técnico.
lessons.situation: Antes de começar uma call, você quer criar conexão. O cliente acabou de voltar de um feriado americano e você puxa uma conversa leve.
lessons.context: Holidays are a great way to connect. On Thanksgiving, families gather and share gratitude. They eat turkey and enjoy a long weekend. The next day, they eat the leftovers. On the Fourth of July, people watch fireworks. Many have a cookout in the yard. Some take a road trip to visit family. It is a good time to recharge. So before a call, I like to ask: "How was your holiday?" A small question builds a real connection.

lessons.title: First meeting & introductions
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz a abertura de uma primeira reunião em inglês simples — se apresenta, apresenta a Racional e os participantes — com um cliente norte-americano novo.
lessons.overview:
The first meeting with a new client sets the tone for the entire project. For Racional, which competes for contracts with clients like Microsoft and Amazon, a strong opening is half the battle. It all starts when you introduce yourself (se apresenta) and say the classic phrase: It's a pleasure to meet you (e um prazer conhece-lo), especially when the meeting is in person (presencial).

In an opening, you present your background (historico/experiencia), explain that you are on the board (na diretoria), and kick things off (da inicio) with the agenda for today (pauta de hoje). It's the moment to set expectations (alinhar expectativas) and introduce your counterpart (contraparte) - the equivalent person on the other side.

The American client values a warm but objective opening: a warm welcome (boas-vindas calorosas), followed by clarity about what will be covered. When you say "I look forward to working with you" and hand it over (passa a palavra) to a colleague, you project the strategic posture expected of a Racional Board executive. That's how you build trust from the very first minute.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "It's a pleasure to meet you.", "Let me kick things off with the agenda." e "I look forward to working with you."

Pratique-as como blocos prontos para a primeira reunião.
lessons.situation: Você lidera a primeira reunião com um cliente americano novo. Precisa se apresentar, apresentar a Racional e a equipe, e dar início à pauta.
lessons.context: Good morning, everyone. It's a pleasure to meet you in person. Let me introduce myself. I am on the board of Racional. Racional is a Brazilian builder with more than fifty years. Let me kick things off with the agenda for today. First, I will give a short background. Then we set expectations together. This is my counterpart, Ana. She runs our project team. A warm welcome to all of you. I look forward to working with you. Now I hand it over to Ana.

lessons.title: Conference calls & virtual meetings
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você participa e conduz conference calls em inglês simples — administrando áudio, turnos de fala e problemas técnicos — com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
A large share of Racional's monthly and biweekly meetings with U.S. clients happens over virtual calls. Knowing how to navigate a conference call in English is now a basic governance skill. The terms start with the audio: being on mute (mudo), to unmute (desmutar), and to share your screen (compartilhar a tela) to show a schedule or a floor plan.

Calls have their own problems. Sometimes people talk over each other (falam ao mesmo tempo), the connection breaks up (fica falhando), there is lag (atraso de audio), or someone drops off the call (cai da chamada). Leading well means inviting people to go ahead (prosseguir) and chime in (dar uma contribuicao), and using the chat (o chat) when needed.

For the Racional executive, controlling the dynamics of a call projects leadership even from a distance. Starting with a round of intros (rodada de apresentacoes), managing the turns, and wrapping up the call (encerrar a chamada) with a recap before we close (resumo antes de fechar) keeps the meeting productive and conveys the organization that American key accounts expect.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "You're on mute.", "Can you share your screen?" e "Let's do a quick recap before we close."

São frases curtas que você usa em quase toda call.
lessons.situation: Você conduz uma conference call com o cliente americano. Precisa administrar o áudio, organizar os turnos de fala e encerrar com um resumo.
lessons.context: Let's start with a round of intros. Can everyone hear me? You're on mute, please unmute. Can you share your screen? We see your schedule now. Sorry, the line breaks up a little. There is some lag today. Please go ahead and finish your point. Does anyone want to chime in? You can also use the chat. One person dropped off the call. Let's wait one minute. Now let's do a quick recap before we close.

lessons.title: Brainstorming & ideation
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz uma sessão de brainstorming em inglês simples — convida ideias, constrói sobre o que os outros dizem e organiza as opções — com a equipe do cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
In complex Racional projects - a hyperscale data center or a hospital with tight deadlines - many solutions come out of brainstorming sessions with the client. Leading that conversation in English calls for its own vocabulary. It starts with inviting ideas: to put options on the table (colocar opcoes na mesa) and to throw out an idea (lancar uma ideia), without fear of being wrong.

The secret of brainstorming is building together. You encourage the team to bounce ideas around (trocar ideias livremente), to expand on an idea (desenvolver uma ideia), and to defer judgment (adiar o julgamento) - remembering that there are no bad ideas (nao ha ideias ruins) at this point. A good idea can spark (faisca/inspirar) an even better one.

After generating many options, it's time to focus: to narrow down (reduzir) to a shortlist (lista curta), prioritize (priorizar), and flesh out (detalhar) the best ones. For the Racional executive, knowing how to open, lead, and converge on (convergir para) a decision projects collaborative leadership - exactly what creates value and trust with the American client's team.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "Let's put some options on the table.", "There are no bad ideas here." e "Let's narrow down to a shortlist."

Pratique abrir o brainstorming e depois fechar com foco.
lessons.situation: Você conduz uma sessão de brainstorming com a equipe do cliente americano para resolver um desafio do projeto. Precisa convidar ideias e organizar as melhores.
lessons.context: Let's put some options on the table. Please throw out any idea. There are no bad ideas here. Let's defer judgment for now. One idea can spark another idea. Feel free to expand on what your colleague said. Let's bounce ideas around. Now let's narrow down the list. We pick a shortlist of three. Then we prioritize and flesh out the best one. Good. We converge on a clear next step.

lessons.title: Status updates (weekly / monthly)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta, em inglês simples, um status update semanal ou mensal a um cliente americano — reportando progresso, riscos e próximos passos com clareza.
lessons.overview:
The status update (atualizacao de status) is the most frequently repeated meeting in a Racional project. On a hyperscale data center for a client like Microsoft, the cycle lasts 18 to 24 months, and almost every week or every month someone from the board needs to tell the client where the project stands. It's not a long conversation: it's a short, factual report on what moved forward, what is concerning, and what comes next.

The American client values directness. That's why the headline first (comecar pela conclusao) technique works so well: you open with a verdict sentence, like "We are on track", and only then go into the details. Next, you show the progress to date (progresso ate aqui) and use to flag (sinalizar) to point out any risk early, before it becomes a bigger problem.

For an Executive Board member, this ritual is also an exercise in trust. Calmly reporting a long-lead item (item de prazo longo) that may slip (atrasar), already with a mitigation plan (plano de mitigacao), shows control. That's how Racional sustains the long-term relationship with its North American key accounts on offices, hospitals, shopping centers, and data centers.
lessons.intro:
Vamos firmar três frases-âncora para usar na prática: "Let me start with the headline" para abrir, "Since our last update, we completed..." para reportar o avanço, e "I want to flag one risk" para sinalizar uma atenção.

A ordem é sempre a mesma: veredito primeiro, progresso depois, risco com plano e próximos passos. Frases curtas, tom calmo.
lessons.situation: Na reunião mensal de um data center, o cliente americano pede o status do projeto. Você abre com o headline e percorre progresso, risco e próximos passos.
lessons.context: Let me start with the headline: we are on track for next month. Since our last update, we finished the foundation. We are a little ahead of schedule on the structure. I want to flag one risk early. A long-lead item could slip by two weeks. But we have a mitigation plan. I will send a short recap today, and I will keep you posted.

vocab.example: Let's start with a quick status update.
I give you the headline first.
The project is on track.
I want to flag one risk.
Since our last update, two things changed.
Here is our progress to date.
The date may slip by a week.
The generator is a long-lead item.
We have a mitigation plan.
We are ahead of schedule.
We are a little behind schedule here.
We report on a weekly cadence.
I will send a short recap.
I will keep you posted.

lessons.title: Hosting clients in Brazil
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você recebe e acompanha, em inglês simples, um cliente americano em visita ao Brasil — do aeroporto ao jantar — como um anfitrião caloroso.
lessons.overview:
This is a lesson about relationship (relacionamento), not grammar. When an American client travels to Brazil to visit a Racional project, the hours outside the meeting room matter as much as the meeting itself. Being a good host (anfitriao) in English is what turns a supplier into a partner for many years.

In an 18- to 24-month project, the client will come to Brazil more than once. Hosting well means taking care of simple things: picking the person up at the airport (to pick someone up), showing them the city (to show someone around), and keeping the first day light because of jet lag (cansaco da viagem). Small questions like "How was the flight?" show genuine care.

Brazilian hospitality is already your edge. The invitation to a steakhouse (churrascaria), always with a no pressure (sem pressao) for someone who is tired, closes the day with warmth. For an Executive Board member at Racional, knowing how to say all of this in English is what creates the long-term bond with North American key accounts.
lessons.intro:
Vamos firmar três frases-âncora calorosas: "Welcome to São Paulo! How was the flight?", "Let me show you around" e "Is there anything you'd like to try?".

O tom é leve e pessoal. Frases curtas, sempre com a opção de descanso para quem chega com jet lag.
lessons.situation: Um cliente americano desembarca em São Paulo para conhecer a obra. Você o recebe, cuida da logística e o convida para um jantar de boas-vindas.
lessons.context: Welcome to São Paulo! How was the flight? You must be tired, so we kept today light. The driver is outside, and your hotel is twenty minutes away. Tonight, if you are up for it, I would love to take you to a great Brazilian steakhouse. But no pressure. We can keep it easy if you want to rest.

vocab.example: It is a pleasure to host you.

lessons.title: War rooms & crisis meetings
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz, em inglês simples, uma war room ou reunião de crise com um cliente americano — mantendo o foco, definindo o caminho e os responsáveis.
lessons.overview:
A war room is the meeting that brings the right people together when something goes wrong on a project. On a Racional project — a hospital, a shopping center, or a data center — an equipment delay or a supplier problem can bring the work to a halt. The war room exists to contain the impact quickly, calmly, and with method.

The American client expects firmness and clarity at this moment. The phrase here's what we know opens the meeting with the facts. Then the group looks for the root cause, sets an action owner for each task, and agrees on the path forward. There is no hunting for someone to blame: the focus is the solution.

For a member of the Executive Board, leading a crisis meeting means showing presence under pressure. Knowing how to keep a cool head, to take ownership, and to set a checkpoint for the next day is what conveys confidence to the client and protects the long-term relationship.
lessons.intro:
Vamos firmar três frases-âncora para a crise: "Let's stay focused" para abrir, "Here's what we know" para os fatos e "Here is the path forward" para a solução.

O tom é calmo e firme. Cada ação tem um dono e uma data; a reunião termina com um próximo checkpoint.
lessons.situation: Um item crítico atrasou no data center e a entrega está em risco. Você abre uma war room com o cliente americano para conter o impacto e definir o caminho.
lessons.context: Let's stay focused. Here is what we know. One key item is late, and this puts the deadline at risk. We are looking at the root cause now. For each action, we will name an owner today. Here is the path forward. I will take ownership of the supplier call. Let's keep a cool head and meet again tomorrow for a checkpoint.

We need a short crisis meeting.

We need to contain the impact fast.
Let's find the root cause first.

lessons.title: Steering committees
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você reporta, em inglês simples, a um steering committee com cliente americano — usando green, amber e red e pedindo as decisões que precisa.
lessons.overview:
The steering committee is the highest-level meeting of a project. It is where the client's and Racional's sponsors look at the overall health of the work and make the big decisions. On a data center or a shopping center, this is where changes to scope, schedule, and budget are approved — not the day-to-day details.

The committee speaks the language of the traffic light: green, amber, and red to show the project health. You report at a high level, without going into technical detail, and you say clearly where you need a decision: we need a decision on.

For a member of Racional's Executive Board, the steering committee is the stage for governance. Knowing how to seek approval, how to present a recommendation, and how to record everything in a decision log is what keeps the project under control and the North American client's trust steady over the 18 to 24 months.
lessons.intro:
Vamos firmar três frases-âncora de governança: "Overall, the project is green" para a saúde, "We need a decision on..." para o pedido e "My recommendation is..." para conduzir.

O tom é alto nível: poucos números, decisões claras e tudo registrado no decision log.
lessons.situation: No steering committee mensal do shopping center, você reporta a saúde do projeto e pede uma decisão sobre uma mudança de escopo.
lessons.context: Good morning. I will report at a high level. Overall, the project is green. One area is amber: a long-lead item. We need a decision on a change in scope today. My recommendation is to approve it now. This keeps us on time. I will add the decision to the log. The technical detail is out of scope for today.

lessons.title: Negotiation fundamentals (BATNA, ZOPA)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você entende e usa, em inglês simples, as bases da negociação — BATNA, ZOPA, leverage e common ground — com um cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
Every contract negotiation at Racional rests on a few fundamentals worth knowing in English. Your BATNA is your best option if the deal falls through — your plan B. The ZOPA is the range where both sides can close, between the client's limit and yours. And the walk-away point is the price below which it is not worth going forward.

Before negotiating schedule, scope, and price for a data center or a shopping center, you need to come prepared. Whoever knows their leverage and their negotiating position looks for common ground and negotiates with the game of give and take, without conceding too much.

The American client tends to negotiate in a direct and well-prepared way. For a member of Racional's Executive Board, understanding the bottom line and the right concession avoids to leave money on the table and protects the project's margin without breaking the long-term relationship.
lessons.intro:
Vamos firmar três frases-âncora de negociação: "Let's find common ground", "This is our bottom line" e "I came prepared".

O tom é firme e respeitoso. Você conhece seu plano B (BATNA) e a faixa de acordo (ZOPA) antes de sentar à mesa.
lessons.situation: Antes de negociar o preço de um contrato com um cliente americano, você revisa sua BATNA, sua ZOPA e o seu walk-away point com a equipe.
lessons.context: Let's get ready for the talk. We need to know our BATNA, our best other option. We also need our walk-away point. The ZOPA is the range where both sides can agree. Our leverage is good this time. Let's find common ground and use give and take. This is our bottom line, and I came prepared.

lessons.title: Negotiation tactics & language
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa, em inglês simples, táticas e frases de negociação — trocas condicionais, segurar o preço e o trial close — com um cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
Knowing the fundamentals is not enough: at the table, you need the right phrases ready on the tip of your tongue. The most useful tactic is the conditional concession: never give something away for free, always trade. The structure if... then... is the heart of it — "If you move the date, then we hold the price."

In a schedule or price negotiation on a Racional project, you will to push back respectfully, show that you listened with I hear you, and measure the space that remains with wiggle room. Sometimes the way out is to split the difference; other times it is to hold the price and to stay firm.

Near the end, the trial close tests the agreement without pressure: are we good to move ahead? For a member of the Executive Board, knowing how to trade, how to lock in the deal, and how to judge when to give ground is what closes good contracts with American clients without wearing down the long-term relationship.
lessons.intro:
Vamos firmar três frases-âncora de tática: "If you do X, then we can do Y" para trocar, "I hear you, but we need to hold the price" para rebater e "Are we good to move ahead?" para testar o fechamento.

O tom é colaborativo e firme. Toda concessão vem com uma troca; nada é dado de graça.
lessons.situation: Na reta final da negociação do contrato, o cliente americano pede um desconto. Você usa trocas condicionais e um trial close para fechar.
lessons.context: I hear you on the price. But we need to hold the price here. Let's trade instead. If you move the date by two weeks, then we can add the extra work. We have little wiggle room left. Maybe we can split the difference. So, are we good to move ahead and lock in the deal?

Let's trade, not just give.

lessons.title: American cities & business hubs
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conversa, em inglês simples, sobre cidades e polos de negócio dos Estados Unidos — conectando-se ao cliente a partir de onde ele vive e trabalha.
lessons.overview:
This lesson is about connection, not grammar. The North American client speaks naturally about the city where they live and about the country's major business hubs. When you comment on their city with interest — "Austin? I hear it is a great tech hub" — you show genuine attention and build rapport before the meeting even begins.

A quick and useful map for Racional: New York and the East Coast concentrate finance; Silicon Valley and Seattle, on the West Coast, bring together the big technology companies — Microsoft, Amazon, and Google, clients in the hyperscale data center segment; Texas, with Austin and Dallas, is growing fast and attracting many new projects. Knowing this terrain helps you understand where the client is coming from and why they think the way they do.

The rule is simple: connect the client's city to their work and ask a short, curious question. Use anchor phrases like "Where are you based?", "I've heard great things about it", and "What's it like there?" In a few seconds, geography turns into conversation, and conversation turns into a long-term relationship with the key account.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três frases-âncora: "Where are you based?" (onde você mora?), "I've heard great things about it." (ouvi falar muito bem de lá) e "What's it like there?" (como é por lá?).

Use o vocabulário do tema — tech hub, booming, cost of living — para comentar a cidade e devolver com uma pergunta curiosa.
lessons.situation: Num café antes da reunião, o cliente americano diz que mora em Austin. Você puxa uma conversa leve sobre a cidade e os polos de tecnologia dos EUA.
lessons.context: Oh, you are based in Austin? Nice! I hear it is a great tech hub now. The tech market there is booming. Many companies move to Texas because the cost of living is good. I was only on the East Coast, in New York. What is Austin like? I want to visit one day.

lessons.title: Hard bargaining vs. principled negotiation
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você diferencia, em inglês simples, a barganha dura da negociação por princípios — falando de interesses, critérios e ganho mútuo com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
As a Board executive, you do not negotiate to win a fight: you negotiate to build a relationship of 18 to 24 months. This lesson separates two styles. Hard bargaining treats the other side as an opponent and only disputes who gives in first. Principled negotiation attacks the problem, not the person, and seeks an agreement that is fair for both sides.

The secret is to separate the position (what each side asks for) from the interest (the real reason behind the request) and to lean on objective criteria (market price, schedules, benchmarks). When the client asks for a hard number, you ask why, look for common ground, and aim for the win-win. On a project with 620+ deliverables like Racional's, scope and risk are discussed with data, not with pressure.

The golden rule: be firm on the problem and gentle with the person. With the American client, who values directness, firmness combined with respect builds credibility. Simple anchor phrases — "What is the interest behind that?" and "Let's find common ground" — keep the conversation professional and protect the long-term partnership.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três âncoras: "What is the interest behind that?" (qual é o interesse por trás disso?), "Let's find common ground." (vamos achar um terreno comum) e "We want a win-win." (queremos um ganha-ganha).

Foque no interest por trás do número, use objective criteria e mantenha o tom firme, mas respeitoso.
lessons.situation: Numa negociação de contrato, o cliente americano abre com uma postura dura sobre preço. Você leva a conversa para os interesses reais e para critérios objetivos.
lessons.context: I hear your number. But let's talk about the interest behind it, not only the price. I don't want this to be a fight. If we look at objective criteria, like market prices and scope, we can find common ground. We want a win-win, because this is a long partnership.

lessons.title: Pricing negotiations
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você negocia preço em inglês simples — justificando valor, falando de margem e concessões — com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
Every construction negotiation eventually reaches price. As a Racional executive, you do not compete on number alone: you defend value. The central idea of this lesson is value-based pricing: showing the client what they receive — on-time delivery, safety, technical quality — and not just cutting cost. When you talk about price with confidence, the client understands why Racional charges what it charges.

You will learn how to justify the price and how to talk about margin and bottom line. You will learn the game of concessions: every time you give something, you ask for something in return — that is the trade-off. You will also see everyday executive terms such as ballpark figure, payment terms, and to lock in a price, along with the risk of a cost overrun on an 18-to-24-month project.

The golden rule with the American client: add value, not cut cost. Directness does not mean automatic discount. If the number has to come down, trade it for scope, schedule, or terms — never give a discount for free. And know when to walk away to protect the company's margin and credibility.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe duas âncoras: "Let me justify the price." (deixe-me justificar o preço) e "We add value, we don't just cut cost." (nós agregamos valor, não só cortamos custo).

Lembre o jogo das concessões: cada vez que você cede, peça algo em troca (trade-off).
lessons.situation: O cliente americano pede um desconto grande. Você justifica o preço pelo valor e propõe uma troca em vez de simplesmente baixar o número.
lessons.context: I understand you want a lower number. But let me justify the price first. We don't just cut cost. We add value: we deliver on time and with high quality. If you need a lower price, let's make a trade-off. We can change the scope or the payment terms. That way, we both win.

vocab.example: Let me justify the price.
We use value-based pricing.

lessons.title: Scope negotiations & change orders
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você negocia escopo e pedidos de mudança em inglês simples — sinalizando o que está dentro ou fora do escopo e o impacto de custo e prazo — com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
On an 18-to-24-month project, the client always asks for changes. The key question is: is this in scope or out of scope? This lesson teaches you to handle the scope baseline and to use the change order: the document that records any extra work, with its cost and its schedule.

The silent risk is scope creep: small requests that no one records and that, added up, blow the budget and the timeline. That is why the rule at Racional is to document up front: each deliverable must be clear, and any additional work must be flagged. The key verb is to flag: you point out early the cost impact and the schedule impact before moving forward.

With the American client, clarity is respect. Say plainly what counts as additional work and ask them to sign off on the change order before it begins. This protects the margin, avoids future conflict, and shows the governance expected of a builder with 620+ completed projects.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe duas âncoras: "That is out of scope." (isso está fora do escopo) e "We need a change order for that." (precisamos de uma ordem de mudança para isso).

Lembre de sinalizar (to flag) o impacto de custo e de prazo antes de seguir.
lessons.situation: Na reunião quinzenal, o cliente americano pede um item novo. Você explica que está fora do escopo e que precisa de uma ordem de mudança com impacto de custo e prazo.
lessons.context: I see what you need, but that item is out of scope. It is additional work, so we need a change order. Let me flag the cost impact and the schedule impact today. When you sign off on the change order, we start. We document everything up front, so there are no surprises later.

We need a change order for that.

lessons.title: Deadline negotiations & timeline extensions
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você negocia prazos e extensões de cronograma em inglês simples — sinalizando atrasos cedo e propondo um plano de recuperação — com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
The schedule is as sensitive as the price. On an 18-to-24-month project, the American client values punctuality and wants to know, in every meeting, whether the project is on track or whether there is a delay. This lesson teaches you to talk about the schedule with transparency: to say when you are on track, when you will fall behind schedule, and how you will get back on track.

You will learn to ask for a timeline extension and to present a recovery plan: how to make up time and adjust the critical path without missing the committed date. Terms like milestone date and buffer help you explain the schedule clearly in a war room with the client.

The golden rule: flag early. Hiding a delay destroys trust; warning in advance and bringing a plan shows control and governance. When the cause is external — heavy rain, lack of material — you speak of force majeure. This is how Racional protects the long-term relationship even when the calendar gets tight.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três âncoras: "We are on track." (estamos no prazo), "There is a small delay." (há um pequeno atraso) e "Here is our recovery plan." (aqui está nosso plano de recuperação).

Lembre: sinalize cedo (flag early) e sempre traga um plano para voltar ao prazo.
lessons.situation: Na war room mensal, há um pequeno atraso por causa de chuva. Você sinaliza cedo, explica o impacto e apresenta um plano de recuperação ao cliente americano.
lessons.context: I want to flag something early. We have a small delay because of heavy rain. But we are still close to the committed date. Here is our recovery plan: we add a second team and we make up time on the critical path. We will get back on track in two weeks.

lessons.title: Being hosted in the US
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conversa, em inglês simples, quando é recebido por um cliente nos EUA — agradecendo a hospitalidade e retribuindo o gesto com naturalidade.
lessons.overview:
This is a lesson about relationship, the human side of each project's 18-to-24-month cycle. At some point the North American client will host you: a dinner, a tour of the city, a visit to headquarters. Knowing how to act as a good guest and how to thank them for their hospitality with genuine warmth strengthens the partnership as much as a good technical meeting.

You will learn to recognize a thoughtful gesture and to say, simply, how much it means: "It means a lot" and "I really appreciate it". You will also learn to give back: offering to pick up the tab with a "Let me get this one" and promising to return the favor when the client comes to Brazil to visit a Racional project.

The golden rule: simple, sincere gratitude is worth more than long sentences. With Americans, a direct thank-you and an invitation for the future — "Next time you are in São Paulo, let me show you around" — turn a business dinner into a genuine long-term relationship.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três âncoras: "Thank you for having me." (obrigado por me receber), "It means a lot." (significa muito) e "Let me return the favor." (deixe-me retribuir).

Use gratidão curta e sincera e termine com um convite para o futuro.
lessons.situation: O cliente americano te recebe para jantar e te mostra a cidade. Você agradece a hospitalidade e se oferece para retribuir o gesto.
lessons.context: Thank you so much for having me. This dinner is wonderful, and the city tour was very thoughtful. It means a lot to me. Let me get this one, please. And next time you are in São Paulo, let me return the favor. I will show you around and we will grab dinner. I really appreciate it.

lessons.title: Difficult conversations & conflict resolution
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue abrir e conduzir uma conversa difícil em inglês com um cliente norte-americano — nomear o problema, ouvir o outro e propor um caminho — usando frases curtas e calmas.
lessons.overview:
On 18-to-24-month projects like Racional's, friction is inevitable: a tight deadline, a contested cost, a communication breakdown that causes rework. The difficult conversation is the moment when a senior executive shows leadership. You do not run from it; you lead it calmly and in clear English, even with an American client who is direct and used to facing problems head-on.

The goal is never to win the argument, but to find a way forward. For that, three simple moves are enough: to address an issue without accusing, to hear someone out, and to move forward together. When the fault is Racional's, saying so clearly — to own a mistake — strengthens the relationship rather than weakening it.

In the daily life of the executive board, this shows up in war rooms and monthly meetings with clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google, who build data centers with Racional. These clients value those who reduce tension and protect the long-term relationship. Knowing how to rebuild trust after a problem is what keeps a key account for years.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar três frases-âncora simples. Para abrir: "I want to hear your side first." Para assumir: "That was our mistake. We will fix it."

E para fechar com solução: "Let's find a way forward together." Use sempre tom calmo e frases curtas.
lessons.situation: O cliente americano está irritado com uma falha de comunicação que gerou retrabalho na obra. Você abre uma conversa difícil para resolver o conflito e manter a confiança.
lessons.context: Thank you for telling me this directly. I want to hear your side first. I understand. The problem was on our side, and we will fix it. Let's not look for someone to blame. Let's find a way forward together. Here is my idea, and I want your opinion too.

vocab.example: This is a difficult conversation, but we need it.
I want to address this issue today.
Please, I want to hear you out.
I acknowledge your concern.
We take ownership of this delay.
We own this mistake. We are sorry.
Let's find a way forward together.

Now let's move forward with a plan.

lessons.title: Saying no diplomatically
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue dizer "não" de forma diplomática em inglês — recusar um pedido, suavizar a negativa e oferecer uma alternativa real — com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
A Racional board executive hears many difficult requests: shorten a deadline, lower a price, change a scope that was already closed. Knowing how to turn down a request without breaking the relationship is a core skill. A blunt "no" pushes the client away; a well-said "no" keeps the partnership and your credibility.

The secret is never to stop at "no." The most useful phrase is "Here's what I can do": you decline the impossible and immediately to offer an alternative. This is to manage expectations — promise what you can deliver and deliver it well. For the American client, who values clarity and punctuality, over-promising and failing is worse than an honest "no" at the start.

In Racional's practice, this comes up every week: a data center client asks to deliver a phase sooner than possible, or asks for a cost below engineering reality. Instead of a risky "yes," you to set a boundary respectfully and present a realistic option. This protects the project, the margin, and the long-term trust with the key account.
lessons.intro:
Vamos fixar três frases-âncora. Para recusar com respeito: "I'm afraid I can't do that."

Para virar a recusa em solução: "Here's what I can do." E para oferecer o caminho: "I can offer a different option."
lessons.situation: O cliente americano pede uma entrega antes do prazo possível. Você precisa recusar com diplomacia e oferecer uma alternativa realista.
lessons.context: I hear you, and I understand the deadline is important. I'm afraid I can't deliver everything by that date. Here is what I can do: I can finish the first phase early and the rest two weeks later. This is a realistic option, and I want to be honest with you.

vocab.example: I have to turn down this request.
We decline the new deadline.
I want to soften the no a little.

vocab.pt: eis o que eu posso fazer
vocab.example: Here's what I can do for you today.

lessons.title: Disagreeing & pushing back politely
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue discordar e fazer um contraponto com educação em inglês — concordar em parte, marcar sua posição e propor uma alternativa — com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
Disagreeing well is an executive art. On Racional's board, you need to push back when a client proposes something that brings risk to the project — a scope change, a cheaper material, an unrealistic deadline. Agreeing with everything seems pleasant, but it weakens the project. The point is to disagree without fighting.

The structure is simple and powerful: first you validate the other person with "I see your point", then you mark the transition with "that said", and then you present my concern is. This lets you to respectfully disagree without sounding aggressive. For the American client, who appreciates candor, this balance between courtesy and firmness is the sign of a serious partner.

In the daily life of the data centers and shopping centers Racional builds, this is worth gold: in a biweekly meeting, the client may insist on a solution that engineering does not recommend. You acknowledge their side — fair point — but you need to stand my ground and offer a safer alternative. Defending the project politely protects both quality and the relationship.
lessons.intro:
Pratique a estrutura de três passos. Validar: "I see your point." Transição: "That said, my concern is..."

E propor: "Can I suggest a different option?" Educado primeiro, firme depois.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião quinzenal, o cliente americano insiste em uma solução que a engenharia não recomenda. Você discorda com respeito e propõe uma alternativa.
lessons.context: I see your point, and it makes sense. That said, my concern is the safety of this solution. I respectfully disagree on this one. Can I suggest a different option? I think it is safer for the project, and I want to share why.

vocab.example: I need to push back a little here.
I respectfully disagree with that idea.
I see your point, and it's valid.
That said, I have a concern.
My concern is the safety here.
That's a fair point, thank you.
I have some reservations about this.
On safety, I stand my ground.
Let me suggest an alternative.
Here I have to draw the line.

Can I suggest a safer option?

exercises.title: 5. Diga em voz alta

exercises.explanation: Validar antes de discordar mantém o respeito e abre espaço para a sua posição.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por cerca de 15 a 20 segundos, faça um contraponto educado a uma proposta do cliente: valide o ponto dele, use "that said" para a transição, diga sua preocupação e ofereça uma alternativa mais segura.

lessons.title: Persuasion & influencing
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue persuadir e influenciar em inglês — apresentar um benefício claro, apoiar com fatos e pedir o aceite — com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
Persuading means showing the other person why your proposal is good for them. On Racional's board, you need to make the case for an engineering solution, a schedule, or an investment. Being right is not enough; you have to lead the client to say yes. The question in their mind is always what's in it for you — and you need to answer it.

Simple persuasion has three pieces: a clear benefit (the upside), proof (to back up with evidence), and a request for agreement (buy-in). Racional's strongest proof is its track record: more than 620 projects, 50 years in the market, data centers delivered for technology giants. Showing real results is more persuasive than adjectives.

With the American client, who decides by data and ROI, the phrase the bottom line is helps you close the reasoning in one line. In a monthly meeting, you want to win someone over and to bring someone on board with the idea. Persuading well, in simple English and with facts, is what turns good engineering into a signed contract.
lessons.intro:
Pratique a estrutura de três passos. Benefício: "The upside for you is..." Prova: "Our track record shows..."

E o aceite: "Can I get your buy-in on this?" Benefício, prova, pedido.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião mensal, você quer convencer o cliente americano a aprovar uma solução de engenharia. Você apresenta o benefício, mostra o histórico e pede o aceite.
lessons.context: Let me make the case for this solution. The upside for you is a faster build and lower risk. Our track record shows this: we delivered more than 620 projects in 50 years. The bottom line is simple. This option saves time and money. Can I get your buy-in?

lessons.title: Business trips to the US
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue falar sobre uma viagem de negócios aos Estados Unidos em inglês — voos, chegada, deslocamento e convites informais — criando conexão com o cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
Many of Racional's key accounts are North American — Microsoft, Amazon, Google. On long projects, it is natural to have a business trip to the United States to visit the client's headquarters or a data center site. Knowing how to talk about that trip in simple English puts you at ease from the airport to the meeting room.

The basics of the trip make for great light conversation: the flight, the connection (layover), the tiredness of the time difference (jet lag), the overnight flight (red-eye). Arriving a day early (to land a day early) helps you rest and be sharp for the meeting. These human details bring you closer to the client; it is not heavy grammar, it is genuine connection.

At the destination come the small arrangements that build relationship: to rent a car in order to get around, to check in at the hotel, and, of course, the invitation worth more than a thousand emails: to grab dinner. Asking your host any tips? about the city shows interest and opens conversation. For the Racional executive, mastering this repertoire turns a functional trip into a long-term relationship.
lessons.intro:
Pratique frases de viagem. Antes: "I land a day early to rest." No hotel: "I need to check in."

E o convite que aproxima: "Do you want to grab dinner?" Leve e amigável.

lessons.title: Presenting proposals & defending positions
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue apresentar uma proposta e defender sua posição em inglês — recomendar com motivos, responder a uma objeção e sustentar o argumento — com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
Presenting a proposal and defending it is the peak of executive interaction. On Racional's board, you need to put forward a proposal clearly and then to defend a position when the client questions it. A strong proposal has a direct recommendation — our recommendation is — followed by organized reasons: for three reasons.

The most sensitive moment is the objection. When the American client raises an objection, usually about cost or schedule, the best response begins with that's a fair question and moves on to to address a concern. Showing that the proposal holds up under analysis — that it stands up to scrutiny — is what gives the client confidence. If you do not have the answer on the spot, saying let me get back to you is better than improvising.

In Racional's typical scenario — a data center or a shopping center of 18 to 24 months — the proposal involves an initial cost (upfront cost) and the reason behind it (the rationale). You need to walk someone through the proposal and to stand behind every number. Defending a position well, in simple and firm English, is what closes deals and protects the project's margin.
lessons.intro:
Pratique a estrutura. Recomendar: "Our recommendation is X, for three reasons." Acolher a objeção: "That's a fair question."

E ganhar tempo com elegância: "Let me get back to you on that."
lessons.situation: Você apresenta a proposta da Racional para um data center. O cliente americano questiona o custo inicial e você defende sua posição.
lessons.context: Our recommendation is this design, for three reasons. It is safer, faster, and cheaper in the long run. I know the upfront cost is high. That's a fair question. Let me address your concern. We stand behind these numbers. If you need more data, let me get back to you.

vocab.example: Our recommendation is this design.
Let me put forward a proposal.
I can defend this position with data.
I recommend it for three reasons.
That's a fair question, thank you.
Let me address your concern.
The upfront cost is high, I know.
Let me walk you through the plan.

lessons.title: Phone calls & voicemails
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz uma ligação telefônica e deixa um recado de voz (voicemail) em inglês com um cliente americano, abrindo, conduzindo e encerrando a chamada com clareza.
lessons.overview:
The phone is the hardest setting in executive English. No face, no gestures, just the voice. That is why Racional's Board needs ready-made phrases for each moment of the call: to open, to lead, to ask someone to repeat, and to close. On a phone call with an American client, saying your name and your company right at the start already conveys control.

When the client does not answer, you leave a voicemail. The message has a fixed formula: name, company, the reason in one sentence, and your number. On Racional's projects, this happens every week: aligning a point on the schedule of a data center for Microsoft, confirming a decision on a hospital, or just making quick contact with the key account. Knowing how to call back and to reach someone is part of the daily routine.

With American clients, clarity on the phone is worth more than fluency. They value being direct. Short phrases like is now a good time? and I'll follow up by email keep the conversation professional and organized, even when your English is still a work in progress.
lessons.intro:
Na prática, três âncoras: abrir com "Hi, this is Cássio from Racional."; pedir para repetir com "Sorry, could you say that again?"; e fechar com "I'll follow up by email. Talk soon."

O voicemail segue a mesma lógica: nome, empresa, motivo em uma frase e o pedido de retorno.

lessons.title: Closing meetings & next steps
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você encerra uma reunião em inglês com próximos passos claros, recapitulando decisões, atribuindo responsáveis e prazos com um cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
The way you close the meeting is what the American client takes away in memory. A meeting that ends vaguely gives the feeling that nothing was resolved. As a member of Racional's Board, you close with a clean ending: you do the wrap up, the recap, and you define the next steps.

Three final moves organize any meeting. First, recap the decisions. Then, define the next steps with an owner and a deadline, the action items with an owner and a date, for example by Friday. Finally, set the next contact: let's reconnect next week. On an 18-to-24-month project, like a shopping center or a data center, this closing keeps everyone aligned from meeting to meeting.

American clients like to know who does what by when. Ending a meeting with every item assigned an owner and a date conveys control and respect for their time. And always close by thanking them: thanks for your time. This care builds trust with the key account throughout the entire project cycle.
lessons.intro:
Na prática, três âncoras: recapitular com "So, to recap, we agreed on..."; definir prazo com "I'll send the proposal by Friday."; e marcar o próximo contato com "Let's reconnect next week."

Lembre: nenhum próximo passo sem dono e sem data.
lessons.situation: No fim de uma reunião de alinhamento com um cliente americano, você assume o fechamento: recapitula o que foi decidido, define os próximos passos e marca o próximo contato.
lessons.context: Let's wrap up. So, to recap, we agreed on the new plan. Now the next steps. I will send you the proposal by Friday. You will confirm the budget on your side by Monday. Let's reconnect next week. Thanks for your time. This was a productive session.

lessons.title: Follow-up emails & meeting recaps
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você escreve um e-mail de follow-up e um resumo de reunião (meeting recap) em inglês, confirmando o que foi combinado com um cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
After a good meeting, what locks in the agreements is the follow-up email. With American clients, this email is not just politeness: it is the record of what was agreed. A written meeting recap prevents misunderstandings about scope, price, and schedule over a project that lasts many months.

The structure is simple and always the same. Open with thanks for your time today. Recap with as discussed and to summarize the key points. Attach documents with please find attached. And close by asking for confirmation: please let me know if. At Racional, this email goes out after each monthly meeting with the key account, recording decisions about the schedule of a data center or a shopping center.

The follow-up email also serves to loop someone in, bringing an engineering or pre-construction colleague into the topic. Written with clarity and simple terms, it keeps everyone on the same page and leaves an organized history, from viability to build.
lessons.intro:
Na prática, três âncoras: abrir com "Thanks for your time today."; resumir com "As discussed, here are the key points."; e fechar com "Please let me know if I missed anything. Best regards."

O recap por escrito é o registro oficial do que foi combinado.

lessons.title: Long-term relationship building
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você mantém o vínculo com um cliente americano ao longo do tempo, retomando contato com naturalidade fora do contexto de uma reunião formal.
lessons.overview:
A Racional project lasts 18 to 24 months, and the relationship with the key account goes far beyond the formal meetings. What sustains that partnership is the ability to stay in touch and to keep in touch even when there is no urgent agenda. This is the human side of executive English.

Reconnecting naturally is a skill. A simple message like how have you been? or let's catch up reopens the conversation without needing a formal agenda. Light phrases like it's been too long and I was thinking of you show that the relationship matters, not just the contract. With American clients, this care is welcome, as long as it stays direct and sincere.

The goal is to nurture a relationship for the long run. Between one phase of a project and another, a data center for Amazon or a shopping center, a brief contact with no agenda, no agenda today, keeps the door open for the next project. This is how you avoid to lose touch with the people you want to see again at the table.
lessons.intro: Esta é uma aula de conexão, com tom mais leve. Três âncoras: reabrir com "Hi John, it's been too long. How have you been?"; propor com "Let's catch up soon."; e fechar com "Let's stay in touch."

lessons.title: Cross-cultural meeting etiquette
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você participa de reuniões internacionais com boa etiqueta, respeitando o estilo americano de ir direto ao ponto, dar a vez e manter a reunião objetiva.
lessons.overview:
Every culture has its own meeting rules. With American clients, meeting etiquette values being on time, getting to the point, and respecting everyone's time. Knowing how to read these rules avoids noise and shows that Racional knows how to work with international partners.

The American style is direct. After a very short small talk first (a light conversation at the beginning), people expect you to get to the point and to keep it brief. In a meeting, it is normal to jump in (to enter the conversation) and to take turns, always using a go ahead (you can speak) to pass the floor. Being direct is not rude: it is what people expect. But it is important to read the room (to sense the mood) so you know when to speak and when to listen.

In the war room of a data center for Microsoft or in a biweekly construction meeting, this etiquette speeds up decisions. Being on the same page and closing each action item (task) before the wrap up is what American clients expect from a senior partner like Cassio.
lessons.intro:
Na prática, três âncoras: ceder a vez com "Please, go ahead."; entrar com educação com "Can I jump in here?"; e propor objetividade com "Let's get to the point."

Direto e respeitoso ao mesmo tempo: é o tom da reunião americana.
lessons.situation: Você participa de uma war room com um cliente americano. O ritmo é rápido e direto; você precisa entrar na conversa, ceder a vez e manter o foco no ponto.
lessons.context: Let's keep it brief. We have a full agenda today. I will get to the point. The schedule is on track. Can I jump in here? Yes, please go ahead. Good, I think we are on the same page. Let's wrap up with the action items.

lessons.title: Storytelling em reuniões
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa uma história curta numa reunião para tornar um ponto memorável, dando um exemplo real que reforça a sua mensagem para um cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
Numbers convince, but stories stay in the memory. Storytelling is a powerful tool in executive meetings. Instead of only citing data, a leader at Racional can to tell a quick story about a real project to bring the point to life in front of an American client.

A good business story is short and has structure. You use the setup (the initial situation) to to set the scene, then you show the turning point, and you close with the payoff (the result). The secret is to keep it short, to make it relatable (to make it close to the listener), and to tie it back to the point of the meeting. For example: a hyperscale data center where Racional solved a deadline challenge, told in three sentences, is worth more than a slide full of numbers.

With American clients, a short and well-tied story builds trust and makes Racional memorable among suppliers. Using a real-life example from one of the 620+ projects shows experience without sounding arrogant, and helps you to land the point in a human way.
lessons.intro:
Na prática, três âncoras: abrir com "Let me tell you a quick story."; situar com "A few years ago, on one project..."; e fechar conectando com "And that is why this matters here."

Curta, real e amarrada ao ponto: é a fórmula da história em reunião.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião com um cliente americano, você quer mostrar a experiência da Racional. Em vez de só citar números, você conta uma história curta de uma obra real.
lessons.context: Let me tell you a quick story. A few years ago, we built a big data center. The deadline was very tight. We changed the plan and finished on time. The client was very happy. That is why I am sure we can do this for you too.

lessons.title: Executive summaries & reporting up
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você escreve e apresenta, em inglês simples, um executive summary e reporta para cima (reporting up), entregando a conclusão primeiro e a recomendação clara a um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
At the top of Racional, no one has time for long reports. Cassio, your routine is to decide fast based on what matters. The executive summary is exactly that: you bring an entire project together in a few lines that an executive reads in thirty seconds and already knows what to decide. When you report to a client like Microsoft or Amazon, the summary is your business card: it shows that you respect the other person's time and that you master the project.

Reporting upward — in English, to report up — is a different discipline from the day-to-day of the construction site. Less detail, more synthesis. The central idea comes first: the bottom line (the essential conclusion), then the two or three points that support it, and the detail stays in the appendix for whoever wants it. On a hyperscale data center project of 18 to 24 months, the American sponsor wants to know only three things: is it on schedule, is it on budget, and what do you recommend now.

The golden rule is simple: the first sentence already carries the conclusion and the request. If the client stops reading there, they already have what they need. That is why you always end with your ask (what you are asking for) — a clear decision, with a deadline. This is how a member of Racional's Executive Board talks with the client's board.
lessons.intro: Antes da prática, fixe três frases-âncora. Comece pela conclusão: "Bottom line: we are on budget and on schedule." Diga o ponto principal: "The key takeaway is the cost saving." E feche com o pedido: "My ask is your approval by Friday."
lessons.situation: Você prepara o resumo executivo mensal de um grande projeto para os patrocinadores americanos, que têm cinco minutos para ler antes do board.
lessons.context: Bottom line: the project is on budget and on schedule. We recommend proceeding to the next phase. Here is the status at a glance. First, the structure is complete. Second, one supplier risk is now closed. Third, the cash flow is on plan. The full numbers are in the appendix. My ask is your approval by Friday.

lessons.title: Email writing — formal vs. casual
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você escolhe o tom certo (formal vs. casual) e escreve, em inglês simples, e-mails claros com saudação, pedido e fechamento adequados ao cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
Cassio, much of your contact with the North American client does not happen in meetings: it happens by email. And in the United States email has rules. What changes from one message to another is the tone and the register: sometimes you need something formal, sometimes something casual. Knowing how to choose shows cultural awareness, and business culture is part of your job as an executive.

A formal email starts with a polite salutation, such as "Dear Mr. Smith", and closes with a sign-off such as "Best regards". A casual email with a client you already know can open with "Hi John" and close with "Thanks". In any case, Americans value a clear call to action: say what you need and when. No going around in circles. On a project of 18 to 24 months with a key account, there are hundreds of emails — each one needs to be easy to read.

The golden rule: keep it concise, state the goal right at the beginning, and end with the next step. When you need to include another person, use the cc; when you send a document, remember to attach it. A good email from you is worth as much as a good meeting.
lessons.intro: Fixe três peças do e-mail. Abertura cordial: "I hope this finds you well." Pedido claro: "Could you confirm the date by Friday?" Fechamento: "Best regards, Cássio."
lessons.situation: Você responde a um cliente americano que pediu uma atualização do projeto. Precisa de um e-mail curto, educado e com um pedido claro.
lessons.context: Dear Mr. Smith, I hope this finds you well. I am writing with a short update on the project. We are on schedule, and the report is attached. Could you confirm the next meeting by Friday? I am looking forward to your reply. Best regards, Cassio.

lessons.title: American business media (WSJ, NYT, CNBC, Bloomberg)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você acompanha e comenta, em inglês simples, a mídia de negócios americana — WSJ, NYT, CNBC e Bloomberg — usando-a para criar conexão com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
Cassio, the American executive reads business news every day. Naturally mentioning an article in the Wall Street Journal or a number that came out on Bloomberg shows that you speak the same language — the language of their world. This lesson is about cultural repertoire, not grammar. The goal is simple: knowing how to comment on a piece of news and return the question, creating an easy conversation during the break in a meeting.

The quick map: the WSJ (Wall Street Journal, or "the Journal") is the reference in finance and companies; the NYT (New York Times) covers the economy with a broader view; CNBC is the live markets TV channel; Bloomberg is data and global coverage. You will hear a lot about the Fed (the US central bank) and interest rates, because that affects large investments — including the data centers that clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google hire Racional to build.

The golden rule: cite the source, make a short comment, and return with a question. You do not need to give a deep opinion. It is enough to say "I saw a piece in the Journal about..." and ask "What's your take?" (what is your opinion?). Shared media becomes common ground in seconds, and common ground is the beginning of a long-term relationship.
lessons.intro: Fixe três frases-âncora. Cite a fonte: "I saw a piece in the Journal about the Fed." Comente curto: "I try to stay informed, but I don't follow every detail." Devolva: "What's your take?"
lessons.situation: No intervalo de uma reunião, o cliente americano comenta uma notícia de economia que viu na CNBC. Você acompanha, dá um comentário breve e devolve a pergunta.
lessons.context: Oh, I saw that on CNBC this morning. There was a good piece in the Journal too, about the Fed and interest rates. I try to stay informed, but I don't follow every detail. It seems to affect a lot of the data center deals. What's your take?

lessons.title: Pitch comercial do shopping center
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz, em inglês simples, o pitch comercial de um shopping center — abrindo a oportunidade, mostrando o track record da Racional e fechando com a sua proposta e o próximo passo.
lessons.overview:
Cassio, this is the first of the three final presentations of the course. The scenario is integrated: a North American client wants to build a shopping center in Brazil and is choosing the partner. You lead the pitch (commercial presentation) to win the business (win the contract). Everything you learned in the previous modules now turns into action: positioning, confidence, and clarity.

A good pitch has three parts. First, the opportunity: why this project matters to the client. Second, the proof: Racional's track record — 50+ years, 620+ projects, 10M+ m² built, including shopping centers and hyperscale data centers. Third, what comes now: your proposal and the next step. The central argument is delivery certainty: with Racional, the client has one accountable team from the feasibility study to the delivery.

The golden rule of pitching to an American: be direct, show proof, and end with a clear request. You do not sell with adjectives; you sell with a track record and a plan. Close by saying that you want to earn their trust and propose the concrete next step. This is how Racional becomes the chosen partner.
lessons.intro: Fixe a estrutura do pitch. Abra: "Thank you for the opportunity. Let me walk you through our plan." Prove: "We have a strong track record in shopping centers." Feche: "My proposal is to start the feasibility study. The next step is a call next week."
lessons.situation: Você apresenta o pitch da Racional para o cliente americano que quer construir um shopping center e está decidindo o parceiro.
lessons.context: Thank you for the opportunity. Let me walk you through our plan. We build shopping centers, hospitals, and data centers. We have a strong track record, with more than 600 projects in 50 years. With us, you get one accountable team and delivery certainty. We want to earn your trust. lessons.title: Desenho técnico e execução do projeto
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explica, em inglês simples, o desenho técnico e a execução do shopping center — o plano por fases, o cronograma e como você sinaliza riscos ao cliente.
lessons.overview:
Cassio, the American client signed with Racional. Now comes the second presentation: you explain how the shopping center will come off the paper. This is the execution phase, and the client wants to see the plan clearly. You will talk about technical drawing, about when we are going to break ground (start the construction), and about how the work is organized in phased delivery.

Racional's model — viability, engineering, pre-construction, build — helps a lot here. You show that the team is going to sequence the work (organize the order of the work), take care of procurement (purchasing of materials) and site logistics, and keep everything on schedule. When something changes, you do not hide it: you flag it. Saying "I want to flag a risk" in advance is what separates a reliable partner from an ordinary supplier, and Americans value this transparency a lot.

The golden rule of this presentation: be clear about the plan, honest about the risks, and firm about quality control. End by showing how you are going to stay on track and what the handover will look like at the end. The client does not need to understand engineering; they need to trust that you do — and that you keep them informed.
lessons.intro: Fixe a estrutura. Mostre o plano: "Let me walk you through the phased delivery." Dê a data: "We break ground in March and stay on schedule." Seja honesto: "I want to flag one risk early."

lessons.context: Let me walk you through the plan. We break ground in March. The work has three phases, so this is a phased delivery. We control procurement and site logistics to stay on schedule. Quality control is part of every phase. I want to flag one risk early: one material may be late. We have a backup plan. The handover is set for next year.

lessons.title: Entrega, avaliação de custos e ROI
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz, em inglês simples, a entrega final do shopping center — confirmando o handover, falando de custos e ROI, e fechando com os próximos passos.
lessons.overview:
Cassio, this is the third and final presentation of the course: the delivery. The shopping center is ready and you lead the closing meeting with the American client. The great moment is the handover: you hand over the finished project. And the best news an executive can give is that the project came in on budget or even under budget and on time.

But Racional's delivery does not stop at the physical building; it speaks the investor's language. You present the ROI (return on investment) and the payback period. You show that there was no cost overrun, you explain each change order (change in scope), and you point out the asset value and the expected occupancy rate. For a client like the ones Racional serves, these numbers are what prove that choosing the partner was the right call.

The golden rule of the closing: confirm the delivery, show the numbers with pride and simplicity, and propose the next steps for the long-term relationship. You close the 18-to-24-month cycle the way it began in the pitch — with delivery certainty and with the trust you have earned. End with "to wrap up" and open the door to the next project.
lessons.intro: Fixe a estrutura do fechamento. Confirme: "We hand over today, on time and on budget." Mostre os números: "The ROI is strong and there was no cost overrun." Encerre: "To wrap up, here are the next steps."
lessons.situation: Você conduz a reunião de entrega do shopping center ao cliente americano: confirma o handover, apresenta custos e ROI, e propõe os próximos passos.
lessons.context: Thank you all. Today we hand over the shopping center, on time and on budget. In fact, we came in under budget. There was no cost overrun. The ROI is strong, and the payback period is short. The occupancy rate looks good for year one. To wrap up, here are the next steps. We would love to work with you again.

vocab.example: The handover is today.
We finished on budget.
We came in under budget.
The ROI is strong.
The payback period is short.
There was no cost overrun.
We had only one change order.
The asset value is high.
The occupancy rate looks good.
We gave you delivery certainty.
We came in under the budget.
Let me wrap up now.
There is a clear value uplift.
Here are the next steps.

exercises.title: 1. Como anunciar a entrega
exercises.prompt: O projeto terminou bem. Como abrir a reunião de handover com o cliente americano?

options.text: We had many problems, but it is done somehow.
options.whyWrong: Tom negativo apaga o sucesso; abra com a boa notícia clara.

options.text: Today we hand over, on time and on budget.
I am not sure about the numbers yet.
options.whyWrong: Insegurança no fechamento; chegue à reunião com os números prontos.

exercises.explanation: Abra com a notícia mais forte: a entrega no prazo e dentro do orçamento.

exercises.title: 2. Apresente os números
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 a 3 frases fechando o projeto com os números. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula, como on budget e ROI.
exercises.modelAnswer: We came in under budget, with no cost overrun. The ROI is strong and the payback period is short. To wrap up, here are the next steps for the next project.
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos: mostre orçamento, ROI e o próximo passo.

exercises.title: 3. Leia em voz alta
exercises.targetText: We hand over today, on time and on budget. The ROI is strong.
exercises.translation: Entregamos hoje, no prazo e dentro do orçamento. O ROI é forte.
exercises.prompt: Você abre a reunião de entrega. Leia com orgulho calmo e clareza.
exercises.explanation: Frases curtas e positivas dão peso à boa notícia; deixe os números falarem.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, conduza o fechamento da entrega por 15 a 20 segundos: confirme o handover on time e on budget, cite o ROI e o payback period, e termine com "to wrap up" e os next steps para a relação de longo prazo.
takeaways: I can confirm the handover.
I can say the project came in on budget.
I can talk about the ROI and payback period.
I can wrap up with the next steps.
I can offer delivery certainty again.

teacher.overview: M7 — Encerrar o curso com três apresentações conduzidas pelo executivo dentro de um cenário integrado — um cliente norte- americano que contrata a Racional para a construção de um shopp…

flow.how: Aluno organiza a apresentação; cheque tempo e estrutura.
Aluno conduz o cenário do início ao fim, em inglês.
Avalie clareza, fluência, vocabulário e domínio; grave.

flow.what: Fechamento · O que eu aprendi nessa lição
flow.how: Feche SEMPRE por aqui: o aluno marca cada 'I can…' que já consegue dizer em voz alta. Ao marcar todos, a aula fica registrada como concluída e mais clara no programa. É assim que toda aula termina.

watch: Priorize a FALA: o aluno deve falar na maior parte da aula.
Varie a dinâmica a cada aula — o roteiro acima rotaciona para não repetir.
Avaliar com critérios claros; gravar para devolutiva.
teacher.richNote: Esta aula tem conteúdo interativo completo na plataforma (vocabulário, exercícios e recap).

pill.tip: No inglês americano, o 'T' entre duas vogais vira um toque rápido parecido com o 'r' do nosso 'caro': 'water' soa 'wárer', 'better' soa 'bérer', 'data' soa 'dára'. Não pronuncie um 'T' duro.
pill.sample: Let me get you the better data on the water meter later.
